README.md:168 documents `rho` as a supported control option under which "the augmentation then inserts ... unsampled extant lineages", and BDI is the default sampler, so this is not a documented limitation. Mechanically, an IS estimator whose proposal has zero mass on every augmentation with unsampled extant lineages targets f(obs, all missing lineages extinct) = L(rho=1) * rho^n_tips, i.e. the rho=1 likelihood shifted by a theta-independent constant, so its argmax is the rho=1 MLE. Numerics (mine, different tree: 24 tips from ape::rphylo(24,0.6,0.2), set.seed(7), crown 3.30; rho=0.7): BDI draws have 0 unsampled nodes on the linear link, the exponential link and the dd model; fhat(rho=0.7) - fhat(rho=1) = -8.560199 = 24*log(0.7) exactly on both links (dd: -8.530 vs -8.560, within its IS noise); BDI fhat(rho=1) - Nee crown likelihood = 7e-14 / 4e-15, and Nee(rho=1) matches DDD::bd_loglik(cond=0, btorph=1, soc=2) with theta-independent offset 0 (spread 1e-14), so the closed form is anchored; thinning fhat(rho=0.7) = -33.06 (sd 0.11, linear) / -33.01 (sd 0.06, exp) vs exact -32.97, while BDI gives -39.63 (gap -6.65, theta-dependent). estimate_rates(rho=0.7, sampling="bdi", verbose=TRUE) returns lambda=0.7188 (closed-form rho=1 MLE 0.7128) with 0 of 18 messages mentioning rho or a fallback, and prints "sampling=BDI (exact)"; sampling="dynamic_fresh" returns lambda=0.8884 (rho=0.7 MLE 0.8516, within MCEM noise). simulate_tree(phy, method="bdi", rho=0.7) yields 40/40 augmented trees with exactly 24 extant tips vs 39/40 with 25-37 extant tips under method="thinning". The cited script also reproduced exactly (0 unsampled; shift 16*log 0.5; BDI fits lambda 0.47 vs thinning 0.68-0.70). No convention misreading applies: both fhats were compared on the same labelled per-lineage density and the rho=1 agreement to 1e-13 rules out a normalisation artefact; the thinning vs BDI difference is 60-100x the thinning rep sd, so it is not MC noise. The fix sketch is sound: the minimal gate on rho breaks nothing, and the sketch correctly notes that the Stadler-transform trick alone would not fix the M-step because the trees handed to m_cpp would still lack unsampled nodes. Severity stays critical: a documented feature, on the default sampler, silently returns a wrong MLE while labelling itself exact; scope is confined to control$rho < 1, which the claim states.

replication.reasoning: The core defect replicates exactly and is robust. src/E_step.cpp:94 accepts an augmentation only if `std::isfinite(log_w) && 0.0 < std::exp(log_w)`; the second clause is false for any finite log_w below log(4.94e-324) = -745.13, so those completed, valid augmentations are counted as `rejected_zero_weights` (line 106) and, when all attempts fail, the E-step throws "maxN exceeded ... zero weights". This cannot be intended: the comment at lines 141-142 says the zero-weight counter exists for w=0 from lambda=0 (logf=-Inf), which the isfinite clause already catches, and calc_sum_w (inst/include/precision_weights.hpp) plus every R consumer (bdi.R:698,798; de.R:75,85,115) max-shift before exponentiating, so finite weights of any magnitude are handled downstream. Rerunning the verifier's script gave the same picture: 60-tip tree kept 40/40 at s=1, 1e2, 1e4 with median lw shifting by -(n-2)log s as predicted, then 400/400 zero weights at s=1e6 and 1e7; n=150/250 natural units kept, n=400 (DDD loglik -1083.6) fails while BDI draws on the same tree give finite lw=-1083.6; dynamic_fresh MCEM returns (0.3098, 0.122) = two 0.8*pars+0.2*center perturbations with loglik NA and no warning, default BDI MCEM returns (0.2046, 0.048), loglik -1083.4; .mcem_warn_estep blames lambda=0. My own variations confirm the cut is model-, link- and generator-independent: an ape::rlineage 39-tip tree (linear link), the same tree under the exponential link, and a TreeSim 40-tip tree under the dd model all keep 20/20 at s=1..1e7 (lw median down to -704) and fail with 200/200 zero weights at s=1e8; the failure threshold is the absolute lw ~ -745 every time. In natural units a 40-tip tree sits at lw ~ -100, so it is unreachable there; it is reached by ~300-400 tips at lambda=0.2 or by small time units (kyr, years). What did NOT replicate is the sub-claim "a downward bias, not noise" of -1.11 nats in the straddle regime. The verifier's own script re-run gave a gap of -0.25 with IS sd 0.35; my 8-vs-8 replicate design on the rlineage tree gave gap -0.13 (se 0.38) with median lw at -743 and +0.06 (se 0.37) with median lw at -745, i.e. zero within noise. The truncation bias is real in sign (rejected trees enter S_completed but not the numerator) but bounded: log(1 - n_zero*exp(-745.13-max)/sum exp(lw-max)) >= -0.005 and -0.037 nats in those runs, because the dropped weights are at most exp(-2..-5) of the survivors. So the -1.1 nats was one heavy-tailed IS draw, and the "within ~10 nats of the cut the sample is biased downward by ~1 nat" statement in affects_validation_how is wrong; the practical damage is the hard failure beyond the cut, not bias near it. Section 5 of my script did not exercise the cut for cem/gam (s=1e7 leaves this tree at lw ~ -702, both methods then fit normally, cem loglik -707.4 vs mcem-bdi -700.7); a direct cem run at s=1e8 with num_particles=4, max_iter=1, max_time=60 did not return within 10 minutes and was killed, so cem past the cut is established only by code reading (de.R:138-151 tryCatch -> NULL -> fhat NA at de.R:245) plus that hang, which belongs to H22/H23. Severity stays major: every thinning-E-step consumer (sampling="dynamic_fresh", method="cem", method="gam", emphasis_pipeline) fails on trees with |log L| > 745 with a wrong diagnosis, while the default BDI MCEM path is unaffected. The fix sketch (accept iff isfinite(log_w); keep -Inf as zero weight; route +Inf/NaN separately) is consistent with all downstream consumers.

replication.reasoning: Code read end to end (inst/include/model.hpp:359-471, 143-212; general_tree.hpp:184-209). Model::loglik has three compensator branches: ep_exp (per-lineage exact via running sums of exp(-beta_D ts_s)), ep_gauss (per-lineage erf loop, different alive set), and the fallthrough "Standard: piecewise constant rates" branch at 420-426 that D+linear takes: inte += dt*n*(speciation_rate_ep(end node)+extinction_rate_ep(end node)). speciation_rate_ep evaluates D once at the end node (D=0 for observed nodes with parent_id=-1; focal D for extinction / augmented-speciation nodes), so the compensator is n copies of one clipped rate, not the integral of sum_s max(0, eta_s(t)) that the simulator (general_tree.hpp:203-209) and README:79-84 define. The verifier's script replicated exactly: hand tree segment [1,4) code 8.55 vs exact 7.425; whole tree C++ -21.34573227 vs exact -19.69573227 under linear, C++ == exact to 1e-14 under exp; on 40 augmented 5-tip trees max|C++ - R(code)| = 1.4e-14 (the replica IS line 424) and C++ - exact spans [-2.8, +4.8] (my draw), beta_D-dependent; beta_D=gamma_D=0 and dd model agree to 3e-14. My independent replicate (12-tip tree, beta_N != 0, independent trapezoid integrator): exp anchor 1.7e-13; linear C++ - exact mean -3.3, sd 6.2, range [-15.9, +6.9], cor with #missing 0.81 -- so the "up to +/-4.3" figure is a 5-tip number and the shift grows with tree size. New fact: on a fully observed 12-tip tree (no augmentation) the linear-link C++ log f is identical (-49.33625) for beta_D = 0.02, 0.05, 0.10 while the exp-link C++ log f (and the exact per-lineage integral) varies with beta_D -- the two links define different D-objectives even before augmentation. Nothing supports an intended-approximation reading: no README/docs text describes the linear D path as mean-field, the comment says "piecewise constant" (true for N-only, false for D which is linear in t), and the author implemented the exact per-lineage integral for the other two links. Not MC noise: deterministic loglik evaluations. Not a reference error: the R reference matches the code's own exp branch to 1e-13 and the hand-tree arithmetic is closed form. Weakening points: (1) the M-step-argmax illustration is sample-dependent -- on my 12-tip sample code and exact both peak at beta_D = 0.05 (generating value), so the estimation-bias magnitude is not established, only the objective mismatch and its theta-dependence; (2) "focal lineage's rate" is precise only for extinction/augmented nodes; for observed end nodes it is the D=0 mean-lineage rate; (3) the exp-sampler cross-check was uninformative (224-299 missing lineages, all log f non-finite under linear). Since link = "linear" is the default (inference.R:677, simulate.R:137, pipeline.R:59) and d/nd are the recommended models, the default fit of every D model maximises a function whose compensator does not match its event intensities: severity major stands. cr/dd unaffected (confirmed 7e-15), so validation study unaffected.

(1) log_sum sign: inst/include/model_helpers.hpp:129-136 computes r = log(prod_)+sum_ and, when r is non-finite, replaces it by signbit(sum_)*Inf. A zero rate makes prod_ = 0 and r = -Inf (a legitimate value), but the fix-up returns +Inf whenever sum_ >= 0, i.e. whenever the zero-rate node is the last `+=` and no lower-threshold crossing has occurred. Part A of the cited script reproduces exactly: A1 single node lambda(2)=0 -> +Inf; A2 zero not last -> -Inf; A3 zero last -> +Inf; A4 zero last after upper-threshold crossing (sum_>0) -> +Inf; A5 zero last after lower-threshold crossing (sum_<0) -> -Inf; A6 zero at non-last node -> -Inf; A0 finite tree matches the hand formula so the tree builder is right. The sign is therefore decided by node position and by an unrelated running sum, not by the model — a real bug, not a convention. (2) BDI E-step: R/bdi.R:686-703 (.augment_tree_bdi) computes logf via eval_logf and weights = logf - logg with no finiteness filter, while the thinning path (src/E_step.cpp:94, 143-144) rejects non-finite log_w and counts them in the denominator (my R2 on a 30-tip tree: thinning returns 200 finite trees with rejected_zero_weights = 10-12 at the same pars where BDI returns 24-31 trees at -Inf). The guard shows the author intended lambda = 0 to be unreachable but only covered the observed tree, not n_tips + max_missing. Part H/F show an ordinary fit from a mild init also drifts to a zero of lambda within a few lineages of N_max (the weighted complete-data objective is maximised by pushing lambda(N_max) toward 0), so the freeze is the typical end state, not a corner. Two corrections to the sub-claims, neither of which touches the one-line finding: (1) The claim's part (C) and fix sketch treat the max_missing channel (bdi.R:508) as "the same defect" and say a divide-by-attempts fhat there "is the same target the thinning path uses". That is not what the thinning path does: src/E_step.cpp:141-144 puts only `rejected_zero_weights` (completed trees with f = 0) in the denominator and deliberately EXCLUDES overrun/lambda rejections as theta-independent computational failures. So the survivor channel (f = 0) is the genuine inconsistency with the package's own convention — it is the exact BDI analogue of `rejected_zero_weights`, which thinning does count — whereas the max_missing channel is treated the same way in both paths; and trees over max_missing have f > 0, so dividing by attempts there would estimate neither L nor the thinning target. The fix should count the two channels separately and add -log P(survivor rejection) only. verified.affects_validation_how: CR fits with rho = 1, cond = NULL use the BDI sampler by default, so: (i) any fit whose start point has mu0 >= lam0 — in particular the default init = (lower_bound+upper_bound)/2 with a symmetric box such as lower=c(0,0), upper=c(1,1), or any box whose centre has mu >= lam — fails immediately (stop_reason "e_step_failure", pars = init, loglik = NA) and would appear as a 100 % failure or, if only `pars` are harvested, as estimates equal to the init; (ii) the estimator cannot return mu_hat >= lam_hat on any tree, so the sampling distribution of mu_hat/lam_hat is truncated at 1 (relevant for small/old clades or high-extinction simulations where the MLE approaches or crosses lam = mu; DDD::bd_ML with cond = 0 stayed just below lam = mu on every tree I tried, so the truncation bites mainly through the M-step proposals and the init); (iii) inside mu0 < lam0 the weights, fhat (= bd_loglik - log((n_tips-1)!) on these tests) and the estimates are identical with and without the fix, so fits that start and stay in mu < lam are unaffected. DD fits do not go through `.bdi_integral_cr`/`.bdi_p_cr` (they use the mean-field ODE + Gillespie path, bdi.R:129-211, 458-483), so this defect does not touch the dd validation except through shared init/recovery logic.

replication.corrected_one_line: In the CR BDI sampler the guard `if (oE2 < 1e-300) return(Inf)` (R/bdi.R:59) has the wrong sign for mu0 > lam0 (1-E2 < 0 there although the integral is finite), and `.bdi_p_cr` is 0/0 = NaN with a wrong I_mu in the critical branch at mu0 == lam0; consequently in mu0 >= lam0 every n>0 hazard is Inf and each draw either errors in uniroot ("f() values at end points not of opposite sign") or — whenever floating point makes (t_cur+1e-15)-t_cur < 1e-15, i.e. most t_cur outside [1,2) — returns spurious instantaneous events, so the E-step "succeeds" with non-constant weights and a badly biased fhat (observed +233 log units on a 15-tip tree, 10/20 corrupted-but-successful E-steps at sample_size 5 on an 8-tip low-rate tree). At MCEM sample sizes (>= 20) the error path dominates, so `estimate_rates(method="mcem", sampling="bdi")` started at mu0 >= lam0 (e.g. the default init = box centre of any symmetric box) returns init unchanged with loglik = NA after 8 no-op perturbations, the estimator cannot return mu_hat >= lam_hat, and `simulate_tree(method="bdi")` at mu > lam returns NULL silently or, on low-rate/short trees, a wrong augmented tree; both links (linear and exponential) are affected; mu0 < lam0 is untouched and the one-line guard fix restores zero-variance weights and the correct fhat offset (-log((n-1)!) vs DDD::bd_loglik) everywhere.
replication.reasoning: Code reading confirms the mechanism exactly as claimed: for mu0 > lam0, d = lam0-mu0 < 0, E2 = exp(-d(tp-t2)) > 1, oE2 = 1-E2 < 0 < 1e-300, so `.bdi_integral_cr` returns Inf for every n>0 segment; mathematically 1-p = mu0(1-E)/(lam0-mu0 E) is a ratio of two negatives and log(oE1/oE2) is well defined, and Nee's p(t) is valid for any lam, mu — nothing in the docs or the map's conventions section restricts the sampler to lam > mu, and the comment on line 59 ("t2 at tp: divergent") shows the guard was meant only for t2 == tp. Hence this is not intended behaviour. At mu0 == lam0 `.bdi_p_cr` is (0)/(0) = NaN (replicated) and the critical-branch I_mu (line 45) integrates to lam0*dt + log(a2/a1) instead of mu0*dt + mu0*lam0*((tp-t1)^2-(tp-t2)^2)/2 (replicated: 1.068 vs numeric 1.795). Everything the verifier reported replicated from scratch (its sections A-F, the symmetric-box run, and my own variations: exponential link log(c(0.3,0.5)) errors 5/5 and MCEM from there gives stop_reason e_step_failure with pars = init and loglik NA; a 30-tip age-8 tree errors 5/5 at (0.3,0.5); an 8-tip tree errors 5/5; (0.5,0.4999) works with sd(lw) ~ 1e-12 while (0.5,0.5000001) errors). With the in-session guard fix, on the 30-tip tree at (0.5,0.3), (0.3,0.5), (0.2,0.6), (1,1.3) the weights are exactly constant (range(lw) width 0) and fhat - DDD::bd_loglik = -71.257039 = -log(29!) in all four cases, so the fix is correct on both sides of lam = mu. Why 'weakened' rather than 'upheld': the sentence "every E-step and every simulate_tree(method="bdi") call in the region mu0 >= lam0 fails" is not accurate. Because `.bdi_integral_cr` returns 0 when t2 - t1 < 1e-15 and uniroot's lower bracket is t_cur + 1e-15, whenever (t_cur+1e-15) - t_cur rounds below 1e-15 (a 400-point grid on [0,4.9): 316/400 t_cur values, all of [0,1) and [2,8), none of [1,2)) f(lo) = -U < 0 while f(hi) = Inf, so uniroot returns a spurious root ~1e-15 after t_cur instead of erroring. The draw then contains instantaneous event cascades, the weights are not constant, and fhat is biased upward: on the 8-tip age-5 tree at (0.05,0.10) with sample_size 5, 14/20 E-steps succeeded, 10 of them with sd(lw) between 3e-3 and 1.9 and fhat - bd_loglik ranging from -8.52 (correct) to -5.63; on the 15-tip tree at (0.1,0.2) 7/20 succeeded, 6 corrupted (offset up to -20.66 vs the true -25.19); at (0.3,0.5) one of 20 succeeded with a 117-missing-lineage draw and fhat - bd_loglik = +207.7 (should be -25.19). So the mu >= lam region does not fail uniformly: it fails loudly or, on low-rate/short trees and small sample sizes, silently and wrongly. At MCEM sample sizes the error path dominates (3/3 MCEM runs from init (0.1,0.2) with sample_size 20 on the 8-tip tree ended e_step_failure, as did the verifier's boxes), so the practical MCEM consequence — fits started at mu0 >= lam0 die at the init and mu_hat >= lam_hat is unreachable — stands; but `simulate_tree(method="bdi")` (n_trees = 1) at mu > lam can return a wrong tree rather than NULL, which the fix sketch should also take into account (the guard fix removes the Inf, and hence the spurious root, in one stroke). Severity stays major: the default init is the box centre, bounds are mandatory and often symmetric in a validation study, and the sampling distribution of mu_hat/lam_hat is truncated at 1. I could not find a small old clade whose DDD::bd_ML(cond=0) MLE has mu > lam in 60 tries (max ratio 0.63; most MLEs at mu = 0), so as the verifier said the truncation bites mainly through init and M-step proposals, not through the location of the MLE on typical trees. Fix sketch: correct, and my run shows it also removes the spurious-root path; the last-segment guard is harmless as stated (P(U > H(tp-1e-14)) <= 1.5e-14).

verified.evidence:
Code (R/de.R): improving is initialised FALSE (de.R:697) and only set for k > 1 (698-702); the stop check needs plateau_count >= patience AND all(sd_vec <= sd_floor*(1+1e-8)) (704-708); the decay sd_vec <- pmax(sd_vec*sd_decay, sd_floor) runs AFTER the check and only when !improving (734-737); sd_floor = 0.01*sd_vec0 (603). Pipeline sets max_iter = 20 (pipeline.R:198); estimate_rates default is 50 (inference.R:121) while its roxygen says 20 (inference.R:75).
Analytic (Part A of the script, pure-R re-implementation of that loop): ceil(log 0.01/log 0.85) = 29 decays are needed (0.85^28 = 0.01056 > 0.01, 0.85^29 = 0.00898); since the k-th decay happens after iteration k and the check precedes it, the floor is first visible at iteration 30, so the earliest possible "plateau" stop is k = 30 even if no iteration ever improves. At max_iter = 20 the rule cannot fire and the SD at iteration 20 is >= 0.85^19 = 0.0456 of initial (hypothesis figure reproduced). At max_iter = 50 the rule can fire only if at most 20 of iterations 2..49 register improvement >= tol.
Empirical (16-tip CR tree from ape::rlineage(0.4, 0.1, Tmax = 8), box [0,1]x[0,0.5], 20 particles, 1 tree/particle, num_threads = 1; an earlier run with box [0,2]x[0,1] and 30 particles gave the same pattern): estimate_rates(method="cem", max_iter = 20): 5/5 runs converged == "max_iter", k_ran = 20, 9-13 of the 20 iterations counted as improving, so the SD at the last iteration was 0.17-0.32 of initial (not 4.6 %; the improving iterations skip decays). estimate_rates default max_iter = 50: 4/4 runs "max_iter", 19-27 improving iterations. emphasis_pipeline(stages = c("bounds","cem")) with its max_iter default: 2/2 "max_iter" after 20 iterations. max_iter = 100, 1 tree/particle: "plateau" fired at k = 48, 60, 67 (and 58, 80, 84 in a first run); 5 trees/particle: 2/2 still "max_iter" at 100 with 48 improving iterations. The improving count is ~half of all iterations because tol = 1e-4 is far below the MC noise of the best-of-population fhat (cf. H42), which is a second reason the floor is reached late. replication.reasoning: The code path is as the verifier describes (R/de.R:696-737): at k = 1 `improving` is FALSE, the plateau/floor check runs before the decay, the decay `pmax(sd_vec*sd_decay, sd_floor)` runs only on non-improving iterations, and sd_floor = 0.01*sd_vec0 regardless of the user's sd_vec (so the ratio argument is invariant to the box). 0.85^28 = 0.01056 > 0.01 and 0.85^29 = 0.00898, so 29 decays (after iterations 1..29) are needed before the check at iteration 30 can see the floor; the earliest possible "plateau" is k = 30 even if nothing ever improves. I confirmed this on the real loop rather than a re-implementation by forcing tol = 1e6 (no iteration can ever count as improving): with max_iter = 29 both runs ended "max_iter" at k = 29, with max_iter = 30 and 35 all four runs ended "plateau" at exactly k = 30 (35-tip tree, box [0,2]x[0,1]). So the pipeline's max_iter = 20 (pipeline.R:198) is arithmetically unreachable by the plateau rule; the pipeline stage with its own true defaults (50 particles x 5 trees, not the 20x1 the verifier substituted) ended "max_iter" at k = 20 in 2/2 runs. With estimate_rates' default max_iter = 50 the rule can fire only if <= 20 of iterations 2..49 improve by >= 1e-4; empirically ~half of iterations register "improvement" because tol = 1e-4 is far below the MC noise of the best-of-population fhat, so 6/6 runs at max_iter = 50 (cr/linear, cr/exponential, dd/linear, two trees) ended on "max_iter". Raising tol to 0.5 (MC scale) let plateau fire at k = 35-38 in 3/3 runs, confirming the H42 coupling and that the floor arithmetic, not the tree, is the binding constraint at 20. Not intended behaviour: inference.R:121 comments "safety cap (adaptive SD stops earlier)" and de.R:504-520 claims the adaptive schedule decoupled convergence from max_iter, but with the shipped constants the stop rule cannot fire under the pipeline's cap and rarely does under the default one; the returned `converged` label therefore carries no information. Severity minor is right: in the pipeline CEM only seeds MCEM (pipeline.R:231-239), and the standalone CEM point at 20 vs >= 50 iterations differed by ~0.02 in lambda / ~0.1 loglik on the 16-tip tree (a precision, not bias, effect). One caution on the fix sketch: deriving sd_decay from max_iter re-couples the schedule to max_iter, which is exactly what the docstring says the adaptive schedule was introduced to avoid; raising tol to the MC scale and/or dropping the exact-floor requirement is the less invasive route.

verified.one_line: `loglik_var` is the bootstrap variance of `mean(lw) + log(1 + m2/2)` (never passed `n_zero_weight`), while the reported loglik is `log(sum exp(lw)) - log(N + n_zero)`; on the same E-step the two statistics differ by 3-26 log-units and the package s.e. understates the MC s.e. of the reported loglik by a factor 1.1 (ESS ~30) to 4 (ESS < 5), which moves `compare_models` pairwise p-values from 0.001 to 0.12 at dAIC = 1.
verified.evidence:
Code: `.bootstrap_fhat_var` (R/de.R:476-489) resamples `lw` and calls `.is_fhat(..., bias_correct = TRUE, K = K)` with no `n_zero_weight`, so the K=2 branch at R/de.R:88-100 runs: `mean(lw) + log(1 + m2/2)`. Verified numerically on one vector: `.is_fhat(bias_correct=TRUE)` = -0.060150 = mean+log(1+m2/2) = -0.060150, whereas lme = -0.030527. The reported loglik is log-mean-exp with `S = N + rejected_zero_weights` (src/E_step.cpp:143-144; R side R/de.R:69-76; BDI R/bdi.R:696-699 with n_valid). Callers: R/emphasis.R:136-142, R/bdi.R:884-889, R/de.R:881-885; consumers R/inference.R:855-856 (print "MC se") and R/inference.R:917-942 (`compare_models` pairwise Gaussian test, `Var(T)=4(v_i+v_j)`).

A. Ratio se_pkg / se_true_LME = 0.99, 0.83, 0.43, 0.28, 0.23. Point values also diverge: at sigma=4, ell_LME = 5.72, ell_BC = 1.69 (true log E[w] = 8.0). For dd the estimates and fhat are identical; only the printed MC s.e. is understated (~10% at ESS ~30 on the observed fit, up to several-fold at ESS < 10) and any `compare_models` p-value built from it is too small. replication.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and replicates from the code alone: `.bootstrap_fhat_var` (R/de.R:476-489) has formals `logf, log_q, K, B` only and calls `.is_fhat(..., bias_correct = TRUE, K = K)`, so with `n_zero_weight` defaulting to 0 the K=2 branch (R/de.R:88-100) runs and each bootstrap replicate is `mean(lw) + log(1 + m2/2)`. I confirmed on a random vector that `.is_fhat(bias_correct=TRUE)` = 0.804412 = my hand-coded bcK2, while `.is_fhat()` default = 1.032476 = log-mean-exp. Every reported loglik is the log-mean-exp: C++ `E_step.cpp:143` (`S = N + rejected_zero_weights`), BDI `bdi.R:696-699` (I checked `e$fhat` equals the LME to 3.6e-15 over 15 E-steps), CEM `de.R:866` (`.is_fhat` with `n_zero_weight`, no `bias_correct`); `bias_correct = TRUE` only ever reaches the CEM search-time `fhat` (de.R:240; H15). `print.emphasis_fit` (inference.R:855-856) labels `sqrt(loglik_var)` "MC se" and `compare_models` (inference.R:917-942) uses `4(v_i+v_j)` for a Gaussian test. So the number shown is the s.e. of a statistic the package never reports. That part is upheld. The `.bootstrap_fhat_var` docstring itself says it approximates Var(ℓ̂_BC,K), so this reads as design drift (the BC estimator was presumably meant to be the reported loglik) rather than a hidden bug, but the consumer-facing claim is still wrong.

What did not replicate or is overstated is the quantification, which the verifier drew largely from single-sample bootstraps at ESS < 10 and from a synthetic lognormal with sigma = 4. With 30 fresh E-steps per case on two other trees (20 tips lam=.6 mu=.3; 40 tips lam=.4 mu=.1) at N = 50 and 200: (1) the package s.e. IS the correct s.e. of the statistic it bootstraps — mean(se_pkg)/sd(ell_BC over replicates) = 0.70-1.27 in all 12 cases; (2) the level gap ell_LME - ell_BC is ESS-dependent, not "3-26 units": 0.14-0.26 at ESS 39-57, 0.45-0.58 at ESS 9-30, 1.1-1.25 at ESS 6-12, and 10-11 only at ESS 2-3 (the verifier's 30-tip thinning E-steps all had ESS <= 10.5); (3) the understatement factor se_pkg / true sd(ell_LME) on real E-steps is 1.1-1.15 at ESS 52-57, 1.3-1.6 at ESS 13-39, 1.9-2.5 at ESS 2-6 — the "factor 4" comes only from the synthetic sigma=4 lognormal (ratio 0.23), never from a real E-step in either run; (4) on the default BDI path (dd, N=100) ESS was 84, the gap -0.02, and the ratio 1.06, i.e. a 6% effect, consistent with the verifier's own end-to-end dd fit (ESS 30.7, ~10-15%); cr on that path gives constant weights and loglik_var = 0 in both runs; (5) the headline "p-values move from 0.001 to 0.12 at dAIC = 1" did not replicate: rerunning the verifier's own script gave p(pkg)=0.002, p(boot-LME)=0.004, p(fresh 8 E-steps)=0.109 (verifier: 0.001 / 0.124 / 0.000) — at ESS ~5 both the single-sample bootstrap of the LME and an 8-replicate ground truth swing by an order of magnitude between runs, so the specific pairing is noise; with replicate-averaged s.e. at ESS 30-50 (se ~0.1-0.18), p at dAIC=1 is ~0.000-0.001 under every variance, so the p-value effect is only material at low ESS. (6) The proposed fix (bootstrap the LME) only halves the problem: se_bootLME / true sd(ell_LME) = 0.60-0.76 at ESS <= 12 in my data, which the fix sketch does acknowledge. n_zero was 0 in every case I ran, so the "second-order ~8%" denominator effect rests on the verifier's B2 simulation plus the signature read; I accept it as second-order. pars and loglik do not pass through `.bootstrap_fhat_var` in any path, so the validation-study assessment (affects only printed MC s.e. and compare_models p-values) stands. Severity minor is right.

verified.one_line: In CEM shared-tree mode (.eval_shared, R/de.R:340-357) the IS denominator for a pooled tree is log q(z|theta_j) at the target particle rather than the density that drew it, which biases per-particle fhat by 1-3 log-likelihood units in a theta-dependent direction on a 20-tip CR tree and moves the argmax particle; the mode is opt-in (shared_trees = FALSE by default) and not used by MCEM.
verified.evidence:
Code: R/de.R:339-357 loops over particles j and calls eval_logf(pars = theta_j, trees = all_trees) then .is_fhat(ev$logf, ev$logg, bias_correct = FALSE); eval_logf (src/loglik.cpp:70-97) returns logg[i] = mdl.sampling_prob(pars, tree_i), and sampling_prob (inst/include/model.hpp:255-328) uses lambda(pars), mu(pars) in every per-event term and in the compensator, so logg(z, theta_j) != logg(z, theta_k) for the particle k that drew z. The drawing density IS cached (pop$log_q[[i]] <- raw$logg, de.R:325) but never read in step 3. The docstring de.R:291-300 ('what matters for IS correctness is that q is evaluated at the same theta_j used for p') states the opposite of the IS identity E_q[f/q] = L, which needs q = the sampling density. n_zero_weight is indeed dropped at de.R:355 (eval_logf has no rejection counts; .is_fhat default n_zero_weight = 0) and bias_correct is forced FALSE (documented in inference.R:84-87 as 'not yet implemented'); with rho = 1, cr, lambda > 0 the observed rejected_zero_weights was 0 in every draw, so those two sub-claims are harmless here.

Sanity: eval_logf's logf/logg at the drawing particle equal augment_trees' output to 0.0e+00. Mode 2 minus Mode 1 fhat at the five particles: +1.705, +3.045, +2.095, +0.601, -1.475 (SE over replicate pools 0.11-0.14 for Mode 2, 0.015-0.25 for Mode 1); mixture-denominator version (log((1/K) sum_k q(z|theta_k))) minus Mode 1: +0.109, +0.015, -0.131, +0.104, -0.012, i.e. within noise. Offsets to DDD::bd_loglik(cond = 0, btorph = 1, soc = 2): Mode 1 -5.671 -4.874 -4.209 -4.166 -4.018; Mode 2 -3.965 -1.828 -2.114 -3.565 -5.493; mixture -5.562 -4.859 -4.340 -4.061 -4.030. So the bias is theta-dependent (spread 4.5 log-lik units across mu), larger than the Mode 1 IS scatter, and changes the ranking that CEM uses to pick elites. verified.one_line: The `-log(2·tips + Ne)` term in `sampling_prob` is not the sampler's parent-choice probability but the exact multiplicity of complete labelled birth-death outcomes per augmented configuration summed over parents (2 per observed lineage incl. the two crown lineages, 1 per missing lineage), so f/q is unbiased for CR and linear-DD whenever f does not depend on the parent; the residual theta-dependent bias of the package's fhat comes from the thinning envelope (H7), not from q.
verified.evidence: Reading (model.hpp:255-328, augment_tree.cpp:128-191, E_step.cpp:19-38): with `tips` = 2 + #observed nodes before t*, `Ne` = augmented lineages alive at t*, n = tips + Ne, and the sampler's parent set |alive_ids| = A = tips - 2 + Ne (crown lineages are not nodes, so never eligible; A = 0 gives parent -1 with probability 1). The hypothesis is right that the three numbers differ; it is wrong that this makes the weight wrong. Derivation on the 2-tip tree: one crown lineage has exactly one descendant at T with probability p1(T) = (lambda-mu)^2 e^{rT}/(lambda e^{rT}-mu)^2; expanding p1 as sum over doomed births along the surviving path gives e^{-(lambda+mu)T} exp(c·lambda ∫p0) with c = 2 (checked at lambda = mu: c = 2 gives 1/(1+lambda T)^2 = p1, c = 1 does not), i.e. every missing lineage attached to an observed lineage carries multiplicity 2 (either daughter can be the survivor), while a missing lineage attached to a missing lineage carries multiplicity 1 (swapping the two doomed daughters is a different point of z-space). Summing over parents therefore gives 2·tips + Ne = K, exactly the code's term; because f (CR, DD-N, M) does not depend on the parent, E_{sampler}[f·K/q_m] = Σ_{p in alive_ids}(1/A)·K·f = K·f = Σ_p mult_p·f, independent of A. Numerics, dev/audit/checks/H5.R (package sampler, 20000 draws, num_threads=1): (A) the code's logg equals my R transcription to 8.9e-16; for m = 1 trees logg_code − log q_true(sampler density with 1/max(1,A)) = −1.386294 = −log 4 for all 5540 trees; for m ≥ 2 the identity logg_code = log q_true − Σ log K_j + Σ log max(1,A_j) holds to 1.8e-15 — so literally q is NOT the sampler's density, by the factor Π A_j/K_j. (B) 2-tip tree, package fhat − 2·log p1: −0.0008 (lambda=1,mu=0.1), −0.016 (mu=0.5), −0.041 (mu=1), −0.138 (lambda=2,mu=1.8), −0.199 (T=3,lambda=1,mu=0.8), −0.113 (T=3,lambda=.6,mu=.5), replicate sd 0.001–0.008: a theta-dependent gap, but NEGATIVE and small, incompatible with a wrong K (a factor-2 error per lineage would give +log2·E[m] ≈ +0.5 to +3.6). Its source: P(m=0) empirical 0.629 vs 0.6089 = exp(logg) for m=0 trees (z = 5.8), and 0.6298 is exactly what the envelope reuse `lambda1 = lambda2` after a rejection (augment_tree.cpp:138; on a 2-tip tree nh(T) = 0 so no proposals follow the first rejection) predicts — that is H7. dev/audit/checks/H5_exactq.R draws z from an exact Ogata thinning of the intended process in R and scores with the package's own f and q via eval_logf: 2-tip gaps become −0.0008, +0.0014, −0.0001, +0.0010, −0.0002, −0.0025 (sd 0.002–0.016) for the same six thetas with mean m up to 6.3 (nested lineages abundant); 10-tip CR tree (brts 10,7.3,6.1,4.8,3.2,2.5,1.7,0.9,0.4), fhat − DDD::bd_loglik(cond=0, soc=2) = −12.794, −12.822, −12.796, −12.837, −12.825 across five (lambda,mu) with mean m 1.6–20, i.e. the constant −log 9! = −12.802 within MC error. (C) Package sampler on the same 10-tip tree: fhat − bd_loglik = −12.826…−12.893 (spread 0.067), 0.03–0.09 nats below the exact-sampler values, again H7's small downward bias. (D) Linear DD, model=c(1,0,0), lambda = b0 + b1·N mapped to DDD ddmodel=1 with K = (b0−g0)/(−b1): package fhat − DDD::dd_loglik = −12.805, −12.832, −12.787, −12.844 across four thetas (spread 0.057, = −log 9!), so the weight is also correct for the dd validation model. My hand-derived Nee formula `nee_lab` in the scripts was wrong by a theta-dependent 1–6 nats and was discarded in favour of DDD; the 2-tip p1^2 closed form is unambiguous and independent of it. The cited tech report (E_step.cpp:142) is indeed absent, but the K term is derivable as above.

verified.one_line: Forward simulate_tree() with rho < 1 stamps dropped extant tips with death age = max_t (R/simulate.R:222), which in the DDD age convention produced by div_tree.cpp:45-51 is death at the crown, so every such row yields one negative edge in $tas (40/40 replicates, min edge -5.996 at max_t = 6), the stamped L-table is inherited by conditional augmentation via tree$L, while $tes is unaffected and no inference path with rho = 1 enters this branch.
verified.evidence: Code: src/div_tree.cpp:45-51 writes col 1 = crown_age - start_date and col 4 = crown_age - end_date (or -1), i.e. DDD ages with present = 0. R/simulate.R:215-223 then does `extant_idx <- which(L[,4] == -1); n_drop <- min(rbinom(1, n, 1-rho), n-2); L[drop,4] <- max_t`. Death age max_t equals the crown age, so the pendant edge length birth_age - death_age is <= 0 for every dropped tip. Run (dev/audit/checks/H46.R, 40 replicates of simulate_tree(pars=c(0.6,0.1), max_t=6, model="cr", rho=0.5)): 40/40 replicates had n_drop > 0; 40/40 had negative edges in $tas; n_neg_edge == n_drop in every replicate (e.g. 33/33, 77/77, 51/51); min tas edge overall -5.996; stamped death age 6 in all cases while the dropped tips' birth ages ranged from 2.67 to 6. $tes was intact in every replicate: Ntip(tes) == number of rows with L[,4] == -1 (15 == 15 in the single-sim check), is.ultrametric(tes) TRUE, because L2phylo(dropextinct = TRUE) removes every row with L[,4] != -1. Proposed fix checked numerically: setting L[drop,4] <- 0 on the same table gives min tas edge +0.00074, Ntip(tas) unchanged at 52, Ntip(tes) unchanged at 15, and branching.times(tes) identical to the current tes (all.equal TRUE), so the fix changes only tas/L, not tes. Inheritance by H44: simulate_tree(sim_object, pars, model="cr", n_trees=10, method="thinning") built its L_extant from tree$L (R/simulate.R:344, .extract_Ltable:404) and returned min edge -5.843 in 10/10 augmented draws; the same call on sim_object$tes gave min edges +0.004 to +0.176 in 10/10 draws. Crown-clade cap: the n_extant - 2 cap does not keep one survivor per crown clade; in 3/40 replicates every kept tip carried the same label sign, so the sampled tes has an MRCA younger than max_t. That is a legitimate outcome of random tip sampling (the reconstructed tree's root is the MRCA of sampled tips), not a defect, but it means max_t is not the crown age of tes when rho < 1. Reach: rho = 1 sim has zero rows with L[,4] == max_t (checked); the `rho < 1.0` guard at simulate.R:215 is the only entry; the GAM survival simulations at R/gam.R:377 and R/gam.R:405 call simulate_tree without rho; every `rho` in gam.R/inference.R (gam.R:366,509,516,778,786; inference.R:384,404,445,523) goes to augmentation, not forward simulation; no file outside R/simulate.R reads tree$L; inference extracts brts from tes (.extract_tes, inference.R:223). So the estimator never sees the stamped column; the defect produces a structurally invalid $tas (negative branch lengths) and a wrong L[,4] column for user simulation studies under incomplete sampling, without biasing any fit. Re-rated from major to minor on that basis: no crash, no bias, one wrong secondary output.

Verified on the same table: tas edges become non-negative, tes unchanged. Optionally record the dropped rows (e.g. attr(L, "unsampled") <- drop) so that $tas can distinguish unsampled-extant from truly extinct lineages; L2phylo(dropextinct = TRUE) will still remove them because 0 != -1. If one survivor per crown clade is wanted (so that crown age of tes == max_t), sample the drop set within each label sign with cap n_clade - 1 instead of the global n_extant - 2, but note that the current behaviour is a valid model of random sampling and the cap only guarantees 2 tips. replication.reasoning: The defect is real and the mechanism is exactly as stated. src/div_tree.cpp:45-51 emits the L-table in DDD age units (col 1 = crown_age - start, col 4 = crown_age - end, -1 alive; present = 0). R/simulate.R:215-223 then stamps randomly dropped extant tips with L[drop,4] <- max_t under the comment "extinct at present" — a forward-time reading (present = max_t) applied to an age-unit column, so it records death at the crown. DDD::L2phylo's own source settles the interpretation: it converts col 4 by `age - L[,4]`, so a death age equal to the crown age becomes forward time 0 and the tip's pendant edge is `0 - forward_birth_time` (<= 0). This is not a convention the verifier misread: the map's section 2 and DDD's format both define col 4 as an age, and `.aug_to_Ltable` in the same file (simulate.R) already treats unsampled-extant lineages in age units (sets -1). Reproduction replicated: the verifier's script gave 38/40 replicates with n_drop > 0 (verifier reported 40/40 — pure rbinom noise, two draws happened to be 0), and in every replicate with dropped tips n_neg_edge == n_drop, min tas edge -5.999, tes ultrametric with Ntip(tes) == #rows with L[,4] == -1, conditional augmentation on the sim object inherited min edge -5.49 in 10/10 draws vs +0.001..+0.035 when fed tes only, and a rho = 1 sim had no stamped rows. The proposed fix L[drop,4] <- 0 gave min tas edge >= 0 and identical tes branching times in 40/40 cases; it also matches L2phylo(dropextinct = TRUE) semantics (0 != -1, so tes is unchanged). Reach is as claimed: the only readers of $L/$tas outside simulate.R are prune_to_extant(tree$tas) at inference.R:228, reached only when $tes is NULL, and doc examples; .extract_brts(sim) on a rho < 1 sim object equals branching.times(sim$tes); gam.R:377 and :405 call simulate_tree without rho. So no fit is biased and the affects_validation_study = false call stands. Three parts of the claim do not hold as stated. (1) Prevalence '13-16% of augmented lineages' is a property of the verifier's tree (first non-crown split at 20% of the crown age), not of the code: on my tree (first split at 2.2% of crown age) it is 0.6-1.7%, and on a tree with the first split at 0.03 it is 0.1%. The over-count per lineage is bounded by the first-split time, so both prevalence and magnitude scale with how late the first observed split is. (2) 'nd_linear(beta_M=0): dlogf = dlogg = 0' is an artifact of max_missing = 1 (with one lineage every affected node has D = 0); with max_missing = 50 the linear D model shows the largest deltas (0.186). - Hard-constraint check: estimate_rates(method = "mcem", cond = NULL) started at the box's upper corner returned mu exactly equal to ub_mu (0.104 and 0.079 in the two runs) — the fit cannot leave the box.
- Survival GAM: when `train_surv_gam = TRUE` it is fitted on 500 LHS points inside this same box (gam.R:371-388), i.e. only in the region where survival is already >= 50 %, so `cond = ab$survival_gam` never sees the high-turnover region it would be needed for.

Mechanism: the criterion is P(unconditional forward sim survives with acceptable size) >= 0.5, which for mu/lambda = 0.9 over 20 time units is 0.013 at the truth; survival conditioning (cond = 1 in DDD, the survival GAM in emphasis) is exactly what makes such regions admissible, but the box is built before any conditioned quantity is evaluated.

(2) Let `.wide_bounds` allow mu up to lambda (currently ub_mu = 0.9*lam_hi only, gam.R:684) and extend the bisection along the mu axis using the conditioned criterion. (3) Train the survival GAM over `.wide_bounds` (or the union of the feasible box and the region between it and the wide box), not only inside the feasible box, so predicted survival is informative where it is small. (4) Document in `auto_bounds` that the returned box is a hard constraint on the fit and warn when DDD::bd_ML(cond = 1) (cheap for CR) falls outside it.

(B) exponential link on high-turnover trees: same exclusion (back-transformed lambda box up to 0.36-0.43, mu reachable only via the exp wide bound and still excluding the MLE). The mechanism and the severity are as stated; `emphasis_pipeline` runs this by default, so any tree whose MLE sits where unconditional crown survival is below 50 % (mu/lambda above roughly 0.3 for long trees) gets a fit biased toward low extinction. The fix sketch is sound in direction; a caveat for it is that widening the mu axis also exposes the thinning sampler to regions where it converges slowly (variation D).

verified.one_line: The NA-particle mechanism exists (E_step throws when fewer than num_trees of maxN attempts succeed; de.R turns it into fhat = NA and elite selection ignores it), but in the tested regimes it fires only where the complete-data likelihood is exactly zero (log f = -Inf for every augmentation), never in the likelihood's support, and CEM estimates with maxN = 10 and maxN = 200 coincide within replicate noise for both cr and dd.
verified.evidence: Code path (as hypothesised): src/E_step.cpp:150-152 `if (E.info.num_trees < N) throw emphasis_error_E(E)`; rejections counted per attempt at E_step.cpp:104-118 (zero weight when log_w non-finite or exp(log_w)==0; overrun when missing > max_missing; lambda > max_lambda); R/de.R:138-152 `.simulate_particle` tryCatch -> NULL; de.R:244-247 fhat_i <- NA; de.R:410-415 elites drawn from `which(!is.na(pop$fhat))`; de.R:659-674 rescue only when `all(is.na(pop$fhat))`. So the mechanism is real. Whether it filters the search: (1) cr, 15-tip tree, crown 8 (ape::rlineage(0.5,0.2), seed 26). augment_trees(ss=5, maxN=10), 10 calls per point on an 18-point grid lambda in {0.2,0.5,1.0} x mu/lambda in {0,0.3,0.6,0.8,0.95,1.1}: NA fraction 0.00 at every point, zero-weight and overrun counts 0.0 per call at every point (dev/audit/checks/H26.log, Part A). The pipeline's own CEM box for this tree, auto_bounds(model="cr"): lower=(0.025,0), upper=(0.857,0.349); all four box corners give 0 rejections in 3 calls each (H26_probe2.log). CEM fits (estimate_rates cr, rho=1, cond=NULL, 30 particles, num_trees=5, 12 iters, box [0,1]^2, 3 reps each): maxN=10 -> lambda 0.262/0.270/0.274, mu 0.033/0.052/0.032; maxN=200 -> lambda 0.268/0.268/0.277, mu 0.036/0.048/0.043; mean lambda 0.2689 vs 0.2708, mu 0.0386 vs 0.0427; valid particles 30/30 in every iteration of every run (history$n_valid), nNA in final population 0 for all 6 runs. (2) dd linear link, DDD::dd_sim(c(0.8,0.1,30), 8) seed 7, N_obs=24. NA-fraction map along K=-b0/bN with b0=0.8, g0=0.1 (10 calls each, ss=5, maxN=10 vs 200): K=23..96: NA10 = 0.00 and NA200 = 0.00 everywhere; zero-weight rejections 1.9/call at K=23, 0.1/call at K=24-26, 0 above (H26.log Part C); fhat10 vs fhat200 agree within 0.7 (e.g. K=32: -44.46 vs -44.22). K<=22: 10/10 and 200/200 attempts are zero-weight rejections, 0 trees, so the particle is NA at ANY maxN (H26_probe2.log). Direct cause: eval_logf of five trees drawn at K=30 scored at K=20 and K=22 gives logf = -Inf for all five; at K=23 finite (-108.7..-218.6); at K=30 finite (-69.9..-103.5). The observed tree itself has lambda=max(0, b0+bN*N)=0 at a scored node once K <= N_obs-2, so f(theta)=0 exactly; NA there is the correct ranking outcome, not a filter toward easy-to-augment parameters. CEM dd fits (30 particles, num_trees=5, 12 iters, box b0[0.05,2] bN[-0.1,0] g0[0,0.8], 3 reps): NA particles per iteration 5.5-7.2 of 30 at BOTH maxN=10 and maxN=200 (valid/iter 22.8-24.1 vs 24.4-24.6); in the final populations the NA particles have median K = 10-20 (< N_obs = 24) while valid ones have median K = 34-53. Estimates: K = 44.1/35.7/45.6 (maxN=10) vs 50.0/42.0/47.2 (maxN=200), loglik -43.70/-43.28/-43.98 vs -43.75/-43.94/-45.26 — overlapping ranges, no direction attributable to maxN. The only regime where a finite-likelihood particle could go NA is the overrun corner (max_missing=1e4 exceeded, e.g. lambda=4, mu=3.2 on this T=8 tree, where 10 attempts did not finish in 5 min because of the 120 s per-call cap); that corner lies far outside the auto_bounds box and its likelihood is astronomically below the optimum, so exclusion cannot move the elite set. Residual (diagnostic-only): fhat=NA conflates "likelihood is zero" with "simulator failed", so history$n_valid < num_points reads as sampler failure when it is a hard likelihood boundary, and the all-NA rescue (de.R:659-674) escalates maxN 10->100->1000->10000 uselessly for a population that is entirely on the zero-likelihood side (200/200 zero weights shows more attempts cannot help).

Parts B1-B4, C, D and E of H99.R all reproduce (|diff| 0 / 7e-15, Wilcoxon p = 0.59, MCEM smoke fine, auto_bounds gaussian box (-3.22..0.224)); my variations also hold: a 5-tip dd gaussian tree matches the README formula (3.6e-15), the peak is at beta_N = 1/(n) for n = 5, CEM + gaussian and MCEM dd + gaussian run, and auto_bounds(bird.orders, "dd", "gaussian") gives lower beta_0 = -4.74 (H73 reproduced on the README's own tree). What does NOT hold is the verifier's inference "the compiled gaussian link itself matches README exactly, so the gap is coverage, not a rate defect": the verifier only exercised the no-D paths of model.hpp::loglik. The D + gaussian branch (inst/include/model.hpp, the `ep_gauss` block at ~393-417, erf per-lineage integrals) accumulates the compensator by looping over tree rows alive throughout each segment and never integrates the two crown lineages, which are not rows; the sibling D + exponential branch handles them by seeding `sum_exp_bE = sum_exp_gE = tree[0].n`. Verified on augment_trees output (H99_dpath.R): with beta_D = gamma_D = 0 the model c(1,0,1) logf under link 2 exceeds the model c(1,0,0) logf by 6.0312 on a tree whose logf is -25.44, and that excess equals 2*sum(dt*(lambda+mu)) = 6.0312 to 1e-12; under links 1 and 0 the same comparison differs by 2.8e-14 and 0. So `f` for every `d`/`nd` fit under the README-recommended gaussian link (BDI is gated off for link 2, so these all score through eval_logf/em_cpp) is too large by the crown lineages' integrated hazard, a theta-dependent error that biases the MLE toward higher lambda+mu. This defect is not in hypotheses.json (H8 covers D+linear, H9 covers tip_start conventions; neither mentions the ep_gauss compensator) and it is precisely what an unskipped gaussian-link test on a D model would have caught. Hence the coverage gap is real but the statement that it conceals no rate defect is wrong, and "minor" understates it: the untested link hides a likelihood error on the README's d/nd examples. (One of my own hand-built trees, H99_replicate.R B'', had unsorted brts and is not evidence; the augment_trees-based check is the clean one.) Fix sketch amendment: in addition to the verifier's tests, the ep_gauss branch must add the crown lineages (tip_start = 0, alive on every segment) to the per-segment integral, and the new test-link.R should assert eval_logf(model c(1,0,1), link 2, beta_D = gamma_D = 0) == eval_logf(model c(1,0,0), link 2) on augmented trees.

verified.one_line: The `tbb::task_arena` in `E_step.cpp:63` and `augment_tree.cpp:221` is never entered, so `num_threads` only sets the grainsize and the range splits into 2^ceil(log2 nt) chunks run by the default hardware-concurrency pool (nt=3 -> 4 threads worked, nt=6 -> 8), while nt=1 gives one chunk and one thread (no pool is created) so the `mclapply` children in `de.R`/`gam.R` are single-core and the hypothesis's "full pool per child" consequence does not occur; the M-step's `task_scheduler_init(nt)` (`M_step.cpp:77`) is honoured only as the first TBB use in a process and is ignored after any E-step, so `em_cpp(num_threads = 1)` runs its `parallel_reduce` on all cores.
verified.evidence:
Code: `src/E_step.cpp:62-65` computes `grainsize = maxN / num_threads`, constructs `tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads)` and then calls `tbb::parallel_for` at top level (no `arena.execute`); `arena` is otherwise unused. Same pattern in `src/augment_tree.cpp:221-224`. `src/M_step.cpp:77` uses `tbb::task_scheduler_init _tbb(num_threads)` (legacy API, header from RcppParallel 5.1.11.2's bundled TBB 2019/2020) whose documented rule is that `number_of_threads` is ignored if a scheduler already exists for the thread. `is_threadsafe()` returns true for every model (`inst/include/model.hpp:113`), so the thread count is not clamped by the model.

Measurements (macOS, 10 hardware threads, cr model, 150-tip tree with ~400 extinct lineages per augmentation, `sample_size = 150`, `maxN = 750`; script `dev/audit/checks/H63.R`):

1. Load-independent thread count (`threads` mode, fresh process, one E-step, then per-thread cumulative user CPU from `ps -M`):
   nt=1: threads_alive=1, threads_with_utime>0.2s=1 (utimes 5.46) -> one thread, no worker pool created.
   nt=3: threads_alive=10, threads_with_utime>0.2s=4 (2.88 [main, incl. unpack] 0.92 0.90 0.87 then 0.00 x6) -> 4 threads ran chunks, one more than requested.
   nt=6: threads_alive=10, threads_with_utime>0.2s=8 (2.53 0.47 0.46 0.46 0.46 0.45 0.44 0.44 0.00 0.00) -> 8 threads ran chunks, two more than requested.
   This matches the range being halved until size <= maxN/nt, i.e. 2^ceil(log2 nt) leaves executed in the default arena.

2. Core-equivalents of the parallel region, (cpu - unpack_wall)/cpp_wall, one process, lighter load: nt=1 0.95 (cpp 3.19 s, threads_alive=1); nt=2 1.84; nt=3 3.39 (> 3); nt=5 4.85; nt=10 4.66; nt=1 again 0.97. Repeat under load average 22: 0.77 / 1.45 / 2.09 / 3.65 / 4.05 / 0.81 (ratios depressed by contention, which is why test 1 was added). Scaling saturates at ~5 cores (mutex-serialised tree copy, H68). n_trees was exactly 150 in every run at maxN = 750.

3. M-step (`m_cpp`, 150 trees x 916 nodes, 5 optimisations per measurement):
   fresh process, first TBB use: nt=1 -> cores 0.92, threads_alive=1; again nt=1 -> 0.96; nt=10 -> 3.11; nt=1 -> 0.92. So `task_scheduler_init(1)` works when it is the first init.
   after one E-step at nt=1 in the same process: nt=1 -> cores 3.49, threads_alive=10; nt=10 -> 3.11. So after the E-step auto-initialised the scheduler, `num_threads` is ignored by the M-step. `rcpp_mcem`/`em_cpp` always runs E before M, so its M-step never honours `num_threads`.

4. Fork path (`de.R:223-262`, `gam.R:803-815` pattern): parent E-step at nt=10 (cores_cpp 4.41, 10 threads), then `mclapply(1:4, mc.cores = 4)` children each running an E-step: with cpp nt=1 every child had threads_alive=1, cpu 5.28-5.29 s (equal to a serial run), n_trees=150, all returned; with cpp nt=4 children also had threads_alive=1 and cpu 5.49-5.53 s (serial: a forked child inherits TBB's market state but no workers and never creates new ones). No hang, no extra CPU. The hypothesis's predicted "full TBB pool per child" is refuted; the `cpp_threads = 1` guard in the R callers is effective, and even nt>1 in a child is silently serial.

Side observation while calibrating (belongs to H62, not H63): with a 20-tip tree, `sample_size = 2000`, `maxN = 400000` and nt=5 or 10, the run appeared hung for >7 min at 97% CPU; `/usr/bin/sample` showed the main thread in `Rcpp::Vector::push_back`/`duplicate1` (the R-side `unpack`) with 9 TBB workers in `semaphore_wait_trap` -- the `stop` race let the loop run to maxN and the result held far more than 2000 trees. At nt=1 (single chunk) and at nt=2 the count was exactly 2000. With nt=1 there is exactly one chunk, so H62 cannot trigger.

Effect on estimates: none. Chunking only changes which thread draws which augmentation (per-thread clock-seeded engines, `augment_tree.cpp:41`, `model.hpp:218`); the M-step `parallel_reduce` changes floating-point summation order only. The defect is resource usage: up to 2x oversubscription for nt not a power of two, and an M-step that uses all cores regardless of `num_threads` once any E-step has run.
verified.fix_sketch: E_step.cpp:62-65 and augment_tree.cpp:221-224: either run the loop inside the arena, `arena.execute([&]{ tbb::parallel_for(...); });`, or drop the arena and scope a `tbb::global_control gc(tbb::global_control::max_allowed_parallelism, num_threads);` around the parallel_for (header `tbb/global_control.h` is present in the bundled TBB). Use `std::max<int>(1, maxN / num_threads)` for the grainsize (H64) or leave the partitioner to decide chunking once concurrency is capped. M_step.cpp:77: replace `tbb::task_scheduler_init _tbb(...)` with the same `global_control` object (RAII, effective even after the scheduler was auto-initialised by an earlier E-step) and drop the legacy header (H67). The `cpp_threads = 1` logic in de.R/gam.R needs no change; document that `num_threads > 1` inside a forked child is serial.
verified.affects_validation_how: With num_threads = 1 the E-step is one chunk on one thread with no worker pool, so estimates and fhat are produced exactly as the serial algorithm specifies. If the study uses em_cpp/MCEM, its M-step will use all cores regardless of num_threads = 1 (after the E-step auto-initialises the scheduler); this changes CPU usage and floating-point summation order in the parallel_reduce of Q, not the estimator. Keep num_threads = 1 in the study: it also removes the H62 stop race (single chunk).

replication.corrected_one_line: The `tbb::task_arena` at `E_step.cpp:63` / `augment_tree.cpp:221` is constructed but never entered (task_arena is lazily initialised; only `execute`/`initialize` create it), so `num_threads` only sets the grainsize: the range splits into 2^ceil(log2 nt) chunks run by the default hardware-concurrency pool (measured nt=2->2, 3->4, 4->4, 5->8, 6->8, 8->8 busy threads) while nt=1 is one undividable chunk executed inline with no worker pool; the M-step's `task_scheduler_init(nt)` (`M_step.cpp:77`) is honoured only as the first TBB use in the process and is ignored after any E-step (bundled TBB 2019 header: "number_of_threads is ignored if any other task_scheduler_inits currently exist", and the auto-initialised scheduler persists for the thread's lifetime), so `em_cpp(num_threads = 1)` runs its M-step `parallel_reduce` on all cores. The `cpp_threads = 1` guard in `de.R`/`gam.R` is effective (children single-core). CORRECTION to the verifier's generalisation: a forked child with `num_threads > 1` is serial only if the parent had already launched its TBB worker pool before the fork; from a cold parent (no TBB use) or a parent that only ran nt=1, a child at nt=4 gets a real 4-thread pool. Effect on estimates: none (resource usage / summation order only).
replication.reasoning: Code: `src/E_step.cpp:62-65` and `src/augment_tree.cpp:221-224` build `tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads)` and then call `tbb::parallel_for` at top level; `arena` is never used. The bundled header (`RcppParallel/include/tbb/task_arena.h`, 'Concurrency level for deferred initialization', `initialize()` only called from `execute_impl`/`enqueue`) confirms the object is inert without `execute`, so the loop runs in the thread's default arena (hardware concurrency = 10 here). `blocked_range::is_divisible()` is `grainsize < size()`, so with grainsize = maxN/nt the range halves until size <= maxN/nt, giving 2^ceil(log2 nt) leaves; with nt=1 the range is not divisible and the single root task runs inline, which is why no worker pool is created. `src/M_step.cpp:77` uses `tbb::task_scheduler_init _tbb(num_threads)`; the bundled TBB 2019 header (`task_scheduler_init.h:83-85`) states number_of_threads is ignored if any other task_scheduler_init exists, and the auto-initialised scheduler created by a prior parallel_for 'will persist until this thread exits' (lines 47-49). `rcpp_mcem.cpp` calls `emphasis::mcem`, which runs E before M, so `em_cpp` never honours num_threads in its M-step. `is_threadsafe()` is true for all models (`model.hpp:113`), so nothing clamps nt. Every primary measurement replicated from scratch (verifier's script) and on a different tree with different nt values (my script), including the power-of-two prediction (nt=4 -> exactly 4 busy threads, nt=5/6/8 -> 8) and the end-to-end `em_cpp(num_threads=1)` case (fresh process ends with 10 threads, 9 busy workers, 1.41 cores over E+M). The one part that did not replicate under varied conditions is the verifier's generalisation 'even nt>1 in a child is silently serial': that holds only after the parent has launched its worker pool (verifier's fork test warmed the parent at nt=10). From a cold parent or a parent warmed at nt=1 the child's `wake_some` launches the never-started workers, and a child at nt=4 got threads_after=10, 4 busy, 2.4-4.0 cores. The fix_sketch's advice to 'document that num_threads > 1 inside a forked child is serial' is therefore wrong as an unconditional statement; the rest of the fix sketch (arena.execute or a scoped global_control; global_control in the M-step) is consistent with the bundled headers (`tbb/global_control.h` is present). The `cpp_threads = 1` guard is effective in every fork configuration tested. Side note: the verifier's statement 'n_trees was exactly 150 in every run at maxN = 750' was not robust (nt=3 rerun returned 599 trees; my nt=10 parent returned 535 for N=200) but that is the H62 stop race, not H63. Severity stays minor: the defect changes CPU usage and floating-point summation order only, not the estimator; with num_threads = 1 the E-step is exactly the serial algorithm.
