triage.one_line: bias_correct reaches only the Mode-1 search-time fhat (de.R:239); Mode 2 (de.R:355), elite re-evaluation (de.R:819) and the final estimate (de.R:866) all use the default FALSE, and .is_fhat silently falls back to plain log-mean-exp whenever n_zero_weight > 0.
triage.evidence: Call-site audit printed by the script: only de.R:239 passes bias_correct = isTRUE(input$bias_correct); de.R:355 hard-codes FALSE; de.R:819 and :866 omit the argument (default FALSE); de.R:483 (.bootstrap_fhat_var) hard-codes TRUE. Numerically, on 200 N(0,1.2^2) log-weights: log-mean-exp = 0.682339, bias_correct=TRUE K=2 = 0.524093 (differs by -0.158, so it does change fhat), K=4 -> 0.6529, K=8 -> 0.68202, K=16 -> 0.6823389 (|diff| 7.6e-10), K>=32 identical to log-mean-exp: the truncated-moment identity converges as K -> Inf, as the hypothesis' property test asks. With n_zero_weight = 3 the TRUE and FALSE branches return the identical value 0.667450 (silent fallback). No test in tests/testthat references bias_correct. Note the K=2 'correction' is not a bias correction of the IS estimator but a second-order Taylor approximation of log-mean-exp (0.52 vs 0.68 here), so search-time fhat and reported fhat are different estimators when the option is on.
triage.fix_sketch: Thread bias_correct (and K) through .simulate_particle callers at de.R:355, :819, :866 (or drop the option, since K=2 is a worse approximation than log-mean-exp whenever weight variance is large); when n_zero_weight > 0 either apply the correction to the finite subset then add log(n_valid/S_completed), or warn instead of falling back silently; add a unit test that bias_correct = TRUE changes best_IS$fhat and a property test of K-convergence (the script's loop).

triage.one_line: mu = 0 at an extinction node yields finite log f (-690.78 per node, from the 1e-300 floor) while lambda = 0 yields -Inf; the E-step then keeps a 1-extinction tree (exp(lw) ~ 1e-290 > 0) but discards a >=2-extinction tree as a zero-weight sample because exp(lw) underflows to 0.
triage.evidence: Script: 15-tip CR tree, 50 augmentations drawn at (lambda,mu)=(0.5,0.3), every tree has >=1 extinction node. eval_logf at mu = 0 (pars[5]=0): logf = -2789.6 (4 ext. nodes) .. -5557.3 (8 ext. nodes), logg finite (-97..-194), lw finite but exp(lw) == 0 in double, so the E_step filter `isfinite(lw) && 0 < exp(lw)` (E_step.cpp:94) rejects them and counts them in rejected_zero_weights; a single extinction node would give lw ~ -667 and pass. eval_logf at lambda = 0 (pars[1]=0, linear link): logf = -Inf and logg = -Inf (q has log(n*mu*lambda) per missing node), lw = NaN, rejected. Part (c): augment_trees at mu = 0 never proposes an extinction (nh_rate ~ n*lambda*(1-exp(-1e-10 (T-t))) ~ 0), so all 50 trees have 0 missing lineages and constant lw = -21.38; the mu-floor convention therefore only bites when trees drawn at mu > 0 are scored at mu = 0 (Mode 2 shared pool, GAM grid, bootstrap), where -690 per node enters the log-mean-exp as a finite but negligible term rather than as an exclusion.
triage.fix_sketch: Pick one convention: treat mu = 0 with an extinction node exactly like lambda = 0 with a speciation node (log f = -Inf, i.e. drop the 1e-300 floor in model.hpp:434 and let log_sum/-Inf propagate), and make the E-step's zero-weight test operate on lw itself (e.g. reject iff !isfinite(lw)) instead of on exp(lw), so the outcome no longer depends on how many extinction nodes underflow. Document in .is_fhat that a -Inf logf contributes 0 to the sum but 1 to the denominator.

triage.one_line: The is.finite filter in .ess_from_lw does not change the ESS value: (sum w)^2/sum w^2 is invariant to adding zero-weight entries, so ess_from_lw(c(0,-Inf,-Inf)) is 1 with or without the filter; 1/3 is not an ESS under any convention.
triage.evidence: Script: .ess_from_lw(c(0,-Inf,-Inf)) = 1; the unfiltered computation exp(lw - max) gives w = (1,0,0) and the same 1; .ess_from_lw(c(-Inf,-Inf)) = NA (the filter's only effect is to return NA instead of NaN when every weight is -Inf). On the thinning path lw handed to ESS is always finite (E_step.cpp:94 already rejected non-finite lw). On the BDI path -Inf can occur: scoring 200 dd-linear trees at K = n+2 gave logf = -Inf for 10/200; ESS = 82.17 over the 190 finite ones, which equals the ESS one would get counting the ten as weight 0. The only genuine inconsistency is that bdi.R:699 divides fhat by length(lw) including the -Inf entries (they are legitimate zero-weight samples there), whereas the ESS silently reports over the finite subset without exposing n_finite; that is a reporting gap, not a wrong number.
triage.fix_sketch: No change to the formula. Optionally return attr(ess, 'n_zero') = sum(!is.finite(lw)) or report n_finite alongside ESS in diagnostics so a BDI run with many -Inf log f is visible; keep the NA-for-all-nonfinite behaviour.

triage.one_line: fhat conditions on completion without overrun (S = N + rejected_zero_weights only) so when max_missing binds the gap to DDD::bd_loglik grows with mu (-0.05 at mu=0.15 to -1.10 at mu=0.45 for max_missing=5); adding the overrun counts to S makes it worse (-1.9), the stop-at-N design has O(1/N) bias that is 72% at sample_size = 1, and the post-stop asymmetry only exists for num_threads > 1.
triage.evidence: Script (10-tip CR tree, lambda=0.5, N=400, 4 replicates, num_threads=1) against DDD::bd_loglik(cond=0, btorph=1, soc=2). max_missing=1000: 0 overruns, gap_code = gap_all = -0.03..-0.19 (the residual mu-trend is the thinning-weight issue of other hypotheses, not this one). max_missing=8: overruns 7..132 per 400 accepted; gap_code -0.006, -0.048, -0.112, -0.306, -0.579 for mu = 0.05..0.45; gap_all (overruns and lambda rejections added to S) -0.006, -0.065, -0.196, -0.476, -0.864. max_missing=5: gap_code down to -1.10, gap_all down to -1.9. So the current S estimates L_restricted(theta)/P_ok(theta), the alternative estimates the truncated likelihood L_restricted(theta); both are theta-dependent when overruns occur and the code's choice is the closer one. Inverse-binomial bias: E[1/(1+G)] for G ~ Geom(p=0.3) = 0.517 vs 0.300 (ratio 1.72), confirming the sample_size = 1 case; for N = 400 the bias is O(1/N) and invisible in the table. E_step.cpp:96-107: an accepted attempt finishing after stop is discarded while a zero-weight one is still counted, an asymmetry only reachable with multiple threads. Default max_missing = 1e4 (inference.R:104) with x1.1 escalation on any overrun (de.R:677) means the truncation rarely binds in practice; it does bind whenever the user lowers max_missing or the escalation lags.
triage.fix_sketch: Author decision: (i) keep S = N + n_zero (least biased of the two) but document that fhat is conditional on no overrun and record rejected_overruns/N as a diagnostic that must be ~0 for fhat to be interpretable; escalate max_missing until overruns vanish before the final IS evaluation (de.R:819/866). (ii) Replace the stop-at-N denominator by (N-1)/(S-1)-style negative-binomial correction, or draw a fixed number of attempts and average over all of them, which removes the O(1/N) bias and makes S well defined; guard sample_size >= 2 for .is_fhat. (iii) Move the ++rejected_zero_weights increment inside the `if (!stop)` guard so in-flight attempts after stop are treated symmetrically.

triage.one_line: Under the labelled-augmentation convention no choose(n_obs+n_unsamp, n_obs) factor is needed: fhat(rho) - Stadler(2009) constant-rate density with Bernoulli sampling is flat across rho (gap -0.02..-0.06 with MC sd 0.03-0.05), whereas adding lchoose would shift it by 2.3 to 9 nats.
triage.evidence: Script: 8-tip CR tree (crown 3.26), lambda=0.5, mu=0.15, thinning sampler N=1500, 3 replicates, rho in {1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.25}. fhat = -13.909, -13.611, -13.495, -13.817, -14.901; Stadler reference (n-2) log lambda + 2 log p1(x1) + sum log p1(x_i), p1(t) = rho r^2 e^{-rt}/(rho lambda + (lambda(1-rho)-mu) e^{-rt})^2, = -13.887, -13.580, -13.443, -13.758, -14.846; gap = -0.022, -0.031, -0.052, -0.059, -0.055 with per-estimate sd 0.003-0.047 and ESS 420-990. Mean n_unsamp per augmentation 0, 1.8, 4.0, 6.9, 9.6; lchoose(n_obs + n_unsamp, n_obs) would be 0, 2.3, 5.3, 7.9, 9.4 nats, far outside the observed spread. Mechanism (code-read): f (model.hpp:459-467) and q (model.hpp:308) both live on labelled augmentations z that name which lineages are unsampled, so the (1-rho) per unsampled lineage cancels in lw and the choose factor, which counts relabellings, is integrated out by summing over z; n_obs log rho is a z-independent constant.
triage.fix_sketch: No code change. Document in the map/README that f is a density over labelled augmentations (unsampled lineages identified individually), so rho^{n_obs}(1-rho)^{n_unsamp} without a binomial coefficient is the correct sampling term, and that fhat(rho) matches the Stadler reconstructed-tree density up to the constant labelled-history offset.

triage.one_line: max_missing is multiplied by 1.1 on every iteration with any overrun, never reset, and the inflated (non-integer) value is carried into the final elite re-evaluation and best_IS evaluation; the x10 rescue is bounded (breaks when maxN > 10000) but the x1.1 path is unbounded and overflows as.integer after ~128 overrun iterations.
triage.evidence: R/de.R:677 `if (result$rej_overruns > 0L) input$max_missing <- input$max_missing * 1.1` with no reset; de.R:813 and :856 pass `input$max_missing` to the final evaluations; de.R:659-674 rescue x10 loop breaks once `input$maxN > 10000L`, so at most 3 escalations from the default maxN=10. Traced run (dev/audit/checks/H37.R, cr model, 20 tips, max_missing=1, maxN=10, 10 particles, 10 iters): rej_overruns per iter = 0 2 8 13 9 5 5 10 6 0; max_missing seen in .simulate_particle = 1, 1.1, 1.21, ..., 2.143589 (=1.1^8), final-eval value 2.143589; the rescue loop never fired. as.integer(1e4*1.1^130) = NA, i.e. with default max_missing=1e4 and a user max_iter >= ~129 with overruns each iteration, augment_trees receives NA (Rcpp int NA) inside the tryCatch. With small max_missing (e.g. 1) the escalation is a no-op until as.integer crosses an integer boundary.
triage.fix_sketch: Cap escalation (e.g. `input$max_missing <- min(ceiling(input$max_missing * 1.1), max_missing_cap)`), keep it integer, record it in `history`, and decide explicitly whether the final evaluations should use the original `max_missing` (comparable to other methods) or the escalated one; document either choice.

triage.one_line: Verbose CEM prints `sd=NaN%` on every iteration for every model because sd_vec is 0 on inactive 8-slots, so sd_vec/(sd_floor/sd_min_frac) is 0/0 there and the mean is NaN.
triage.evidence: R/inference.R:421 `sd_vec <- (upper_bound - lower_bound) / 4` on the 8-element bounds whose inactive slots are pinned to [0,0] (inference.R:752-753); de.R:603 `sd_floor <- sd_vec * sd_min_frac`; de.R:745 `mean(sd_vec / (sd_floor / sd_min_frac))`. dev/audit/checks/H38.R output: every line of both a cr fit and a dd fit reads `... sd=NaN%` (e.g. `Iter   1/4  best_lw=-40.0728  valid=10/10  plateau=0/5  sd=NaN%`). Only cosmetic: the stop rule at de.R:705 uses `all(sd_vec <= sd_floor*(1+1e-8))`, which is TRUE on the 0 slots and unaffected.
triage.fix_sketch: Keep the initial sd_vec (`sd_init <- sd_vec`) and compute `sd_frac <- mean((sd_vec / sd_init)[sd_init > 0])`; same fix for the legacy branch `mean(sd_vec/(sd_vec+alpha))`, which is also 0/0 on inactive slots.

triage.one_line: The projected-time budget in estimate_likelihood_surface is enforced only on the sequential branch; the mclapply branch (num_threads>1, sample_size>=10, n_pts>=num_threads) ignores max_time, and when the sequential check fires it stops with an error so no partial surface survives, and the pipeline's tryCatch turns that into a failed GAM stage.
triage.evidence: R/gam.R:808-823: `.check_time_budget(t0_grid, i, n_pts, max_time, ...)` is called only inside the `else` (sequential) loop; the `mclapply` branch at 810-823 has no time logic. R/inference.R:151-166 `.check_time_budget` calls `stop()`. R/inference.R:512-525 `.run_gam` calls `estimate_likelihood_surface` without tryCatch; R/pipeline.R:178-185 wraps `estimate_rates(method='gam')` in tryCatch returning NULL ("GAM FAILED"). dev/audit/checks/H39.R (16-point cr grid, sample_size=10, max_time=0.001): num_threads=1 -> `ERROR: Time budget exceeded: completed 3/16 grid points ...`; num_threads=2 -> `surface with 16 rows, 16 finite` in 0.08 s.
triage.fix_sketch: Apply the budget on both paths (e.g. chunk the mclapply over batches of num_threads points and call .check_time_budget after each batch, or pass a deadline into eval_one_point), and make the check return the partial surface with a warning/attribute instead of stop() so .run_gam can fit the GAM on the points already evaluated when n_valid >= 10.

triage.one_line: The two tolerances are in different metrics as stated: the M-step stops on NLopt xtol_rel=1e-3 relative to |x| per coordinate (near-zero slopes need absolute steps ~1e-3*|slope|, e.g. 5e-6 for a slope of 0.005), while the EM rule stops on max_j |delta_j|/(ub_j-lb_j) < tol=1e-3 relative to the bound range; whether the M-step is meant to sit below the EM threshold is not decided anywhere in the code.
triage.evidence: src/M_step.cpp:81 `nlopt.set_xtol_rel(xtol_rel)` is the only stopping criterion set (no xtol_abs, ftol, maxeval); src/rsbplx.cpp wraps real NLopt (remp_set_xtol_rel), whose relstop is |Δx| < reltol*(|x_old|+|x_new|)/2, so the effective absolute tolerance scales with the coordinate's magnitude. R/emphasis.R:28-29,93 and the BDI driver use `delta_max <- max(abs(pars - prev_pars)/range_vec)` with `tol=1e-3` (inference.R:117-119 defaults xtol=1e-3, tol=1e-3). No comment or code relates the two; for beta_0 ~ 1 with a range ~1 they coincide, for a slope of ~0.005 in a range of 0.1 the M-step tolerance (5e-6) is 20x finer than the EM threshold (1e-4). Not run (the xtol=1e-6 rerun is a multi-fit MCEM comparison, above the budget); decided from code.
triage.fix_sketch: Author decision: either set both in the same metric (e.g. add `nlopt.set_xtol_abs(xtol * (ub - lb))` so the M-step tolerance is a fraction of the bound range like `tol`), or document that xtol is relative to |x| and that the M-step should be at least ~10x tighter than tol in every coordinate, and add a maxeval guard so a coordinate crossing zero cannot stall SBPLX.

triage.one_line: For the gaussian link init_pars is the raw compact bound midpoint (slopes included) with no clamping, because the slope-to-zero logic and .validate_linear_init_pars are gated on link_int == 0L; the code contains no reasoning about where the gaussian rate beta0*exp(-(eta_cov-1)^2/2) should start, so whether the midpoint is sensible depends entirely on the user's slope bounds.
triage.evidence: R/inference.R:714-727: `init_pars <- (lower_bound + upper_bound)/2` and the slope clamp runs only `if (link_int == 0L && any(model_bin != 0L))`; inference.R:731-735 the validator is also `link_int == 0L` only. inst/include/model.hpp:127-130 `gaussian_rate(intercept, eta_cov) = intercept*exp(-0.5*(eta_cov-1)^2)` with eta_cov = covariate terms only (model.hpp:150-153, 160-163, 193-196, 204-207). Consequences from the formula: rates are always > 0 so the linear-link motivation for clamping (lambda -> 0) does not apply, but at the midpoint the CR rate is beta0*e^{-1/2} = 0.61*beta0 (not beta0), and a symmetric slope box gives eta_cov=0 while a positive box gives e.g. beta_N=0.25 at N~20 -> eta_cov=5 -> rate factor e^{-8}~3e-4, i.e. a near-zero start. Not run (counting max_iter stops over gaussian fits from two starts is a multi-fit MCEM study beyond the budget).
triage.fix_sketch: Author decision: choose a link-aware start, e.g. slopes such that eta_cov ~ 1 at the tree's typical covariate value (or 0 if that is outside bounds) and intercept = midpoint*e^{1/2} clamped to bounds; alternatively route gaussian fits through the CEM point as init like the pipeline does, and say so in the docs.

triage.one_line: Plateau detection compares best fhat between iterations, but every particle's fhat is reset and re-drawn each iteration (with 1-5 trees), and on an identical population the best fhat moves by sd 0.9 (1 tree) or 0.24 (5-20 trees) between re-draws, 3-4 orders of magnitude above tol=1e-4, so `improvement >= tol` is decided by MC noise rather than by the search.
triage.evidence: R/de.R:698-702 `improvement <- best_loglik[k] - best_loglik[k-1]; improving <- improvement >= tol`; de.R:418 `elite_fhat <- rep(NA_real_, k)  # always re-evaluate`, so no fhat is carried over; defaults num_trees=1 (inference.R:126), pipeline num_trees=5 (pipeline.R:198), tol=1e-4. dev/audit/checks/H42.R (cr, 20 tips, 50 particles in [0,1.5]x[0,1], same population evaluated 10 times via .eval_particles): best fhat sd = 0.915 / 0.237 / 0.248 and range 2.68 / 0.75 / 0.77 for sample_size 1 / 5 / 20. Under this noise `improving` is essentially a coin flip, so plateau_count and the SD decay (which only runs when !improving, de.R:733-737) are driven by noise; the adaptive stop still requires sd at floor, so this mostly randomises the annealing speed rather than the stop itself.
triage.fix_sketch: Author decision on the intended plateau statistic: e.g. compare a smoothed quantity (mean of elite fhats, or an exponential moving average of best), scale tol to the observed MC sd (bootstrap of the elite's lw, already available via .bootstrap_fhat_var), or drive decay on the spread of elite parameters rather than on fhat improvement; document that with num_trees=1 fhat is a single log-weight.

triage.one_line: Inactive 8-element slots stay exactly 0 in every CEM particle, best_pars, obtained_estim and every MCEM M-step estimate: CEM's perturbation returns the bound when upper == lower and runif(0,0) is 0, and SBPLX starts from an exact-0 slot with lb=ub=0 (NLopt eliminates equal-bound dimensions and returns lb exactly).
triage.evidence: R/de.R:382 `.perturb_value`: `if (upper == lower) return(upper)`; de.R:188 `runif(min=0,max=0)` = 0; de.R:837-838 the softmax mean of exact-0 columns is 0; inference.R:752-754 lb8/ub8/ip8 expand inactive slots to 0 via .expand_pars (simulate.R:298-310). dev/audit/checks/H43.R: CEM cr final_pop$pars, best_pars, obtained_estim; MCEM cr (4 M-steps, bdi sampling) par2,3,4,6,7,8; MCEM dd par3,4,7,8; CEM dd final_pop -> all `inactive cols exactly 0: TRUE, max|.|= 0`. Note the guarantee for the M-step rests on NLopt's equal-bound handling plus the exact-0 start; in CEM it rests on the bound test in .perturb_value.
triage.fix_sketch: No change needed; optionally add a cheap assertion in .contract_pars (or a unit test) that inactive slots of pars8 are exactly 0, so any future change to bound expansion or perturbation is caught.

triage.one_line: The abort/assert symbols are real in the built emphasis.so, but they are NDEBUG-gated library code (Rcpp r_cast.h, Boost cpp_dec_float) compiled in only because pkgbuild's debug build (-UNDEBUG -O0) left objects in src/ that R CMD check and R CMD INSTALL then reused; a clean build has neither, and the one assert is unreachable from E_step.cpp.
triage.evidence: nm src/emphasis.so and the scratch-library emphasis.so both show `U ___assert_rtn` and `U _abort` (identical 1513304-byte binaries; install.log says `make: Nothing to be done for all`, i.e. it reused src/*.o). objdump -d -r attribution: ___assert_rtn is referenced only from boost::multiprecision::cpp_dec_float<100>::operator=(double) and default_ops::hyp0F0 (BH header pulled in by inst/include/precision_weights.hpp); the string `!(boost::math::isnan)(f) && !(boost::math::isinf)(f)` is the assert text. Bare _abort is referenced only from Rcpp::internal::basic_cast<10/13/14> and r_true_cast<16>, which are Rcpp/r_cast.h:70-74 and :126-128, both inside `#ifndef NDEBUG`. Package sources contain no assert( call (only `#include <cassert>` in augment_tree.cpp) and no abort(). R's Makeconf ALL_CPPFLAGS always adds -DNDEBUG, but the recorded compile line in ~/.claude/jobs/867af780/tmp/emphasis-doc-test.log:32 reads `... -DNDEBUG ... -UNDEBUG -g -O0` under `Re-compiling emphasis (debug build)` (pkgbuild), and dwarfdump shows 0 DW_AT_APPLE_optimized units in src/E_step.o. The March 00check.log (emphasis.Rcheck/00check.log:15-18) already reports `Subdirectory 'emphasis/src' contains apparent object files/libraries` before the compiled-code WARNING at :108-118, so that check likewise reused the debug objects. Reachability: calc_sum_w (precision_weights.hpp) receives only log-weights that passed `std::isfinite(log_w)` at src/E_step.cpp:94 and max_log_w is their max, so the cpp_dec_float(double) NaN/Inf assert cannot fire from the E-step; the Rcpp abort fires only on an R-side type mismatch and only in a non-NDEBUG build.
triage.fix_sketch: Never run R CMD check / INSTALL over a tree containing pkgbuild debug objects: delete src/*.o and src/*.so (add them to .Rbuildignore and .gitignore) and check from `R CMD build` output, which recompiles with R's -DNDEBUG; the WARNING then disappears. For belt-and-braces, add `PKG_CPPFLAGS = -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS` to src/Makevars and Makevars.win so BH asserts are compiled out regardless of NDEBUG. Optionally guard calc_sum_w with an explicit std::isfinite check on `exponent` so the Boost precondition is documented at the call site.

triage.one_line: simulate_tree() returns under the single name `log_q` whichever proposal density ran (BDI Gillespie logg from R/bdi.R, or C++ sampling_prob from inst/include/model.hpp:255-328); on a fixed augmented tree the two differ by a theta-dependent amount, and the output carries no field saying which one it is, including after the silent bdi->thinning fallback at R/simulate.R:345.
triage.evidence: Code: R/simulate.R:380 `log_q <- aug$logg` where `aug` is either `.augment_tree_bdi` (R Gillespie logg, bdi.R:440-506; eval_logf's logg explicitly discarded at bdi.R:685-691) or `.augment_tree_internal` (C++ sampling_prob). Docs at simulate.R:55-63 describe both as `log q(z | obs, theta)` with no method qualifier; the return list is `list(trees, log_q)` / `list(tas, log_q)` only. Script /Users/pancho/Code/emphasis/dev/audit/checks/H93.R (log H93.log), 20-tip rphylo CR tree, theta1=(0.5,0.3): (a) same tree/theta, log_q mean -44.58 (sd 10.67) for bdi vs -38.58 (sd 13.21) for thinning; (b) re-implemented CR BDI density matches package logg to 6e-13; on 40 fixed BDI draws, logg_thin - logg_bdi at theta1 ranges [-3.84, 1.60] and its change from theta1 to theta2=(0.7,0.2) ranges [-1.22, 1.74] with cor 0.77 to n_missing, i.e. NOT a theta-independent constant; logf - logg_bdi has sd 2e-13 across draws (zero-variance CR property holds for the BDI pairing); (c) method='bdi' with link='gaussian' -> .bdi_supported FALSE, silently returns thinning log_q, names still `trees,log_q`, no `method` field. Design answer from the code: each `log_q` is the density of its own sampler and the package never mixes them internally (bdi.R pairs its trees with its own logg; thinning paths use sampling_prob), so this is an API-labelling inconsistency, not an estimator defect; whether either q is exactly correct is H57/H8/H9.
triage.fix_sketch: Record the sampler actually used in the simulate_tree() return value (e.g. `method = "bdi"|"thinning"`, or an attribute on `log_q`), emit a message/warning when `method = "bdi"` falls back to thinning at simulate.R:345, and in the roxygen for `log_q` (simulate.R:55-63) state that it is the log-density of the proposal named in `method` and that BDI and thinning values are not comparable across methods (only each with its own draws). Optionally also expose the raw C++ data frames alongside `tas` so users can recompute either density with eval_logf.

triage.one_line: rho is never validated: estimate_rates(control=list(rho=80)) runs to completion under mcem/bdi, mcem/dynamic_fresh and cem, the C++ Model silently resets any rho outside (0,1] to 1, and the forward simulator skips tip-dropping for rho>1 while rho<0 raises an rbinom 'NAs produced' warning.

triage.one_line: The unfloored `fhat - log(p_tree)` in .run_gam would drop a grid row only if predict_survival returned exactly 0, and mgcv's binomial linkinv clamps the response to >= .Machine$double.eps, so the row-dropping path is unreachable; the 1e-300 floor in cond_fun is inert for the same reason and the two paths agree numerically.
triage.evidence: Code: R/inference.R:527-530 `surface$fhat <- surface$fhat - log(p_tree)` then `is.finite` filter at :532 and again in train_likelihood_GAM (R/gam.R:871); R/inference.R:342 `log(max(p_tree, 1e-300))`. dev/audit/checks/H80.R: arithmetic shows p=0 -> gam_path=Inf (dropped) vs cond_path=668.8, but a binomial mgcv GAM fitted on perfectly separated data and predicted far outside the data returns 2.220446e-16 at every point (any exact zero: FALSE; min 2.22e-16) -- mgcv's binomial()$linkinv floors at eps. For any p >= 1e-300 the two formulas are identical, so CEM/MCEM and GAM see the same penalty. predict_survival (R/gam.R:80) is a plain predict(type='response') with no extra transformation.

(An invalid model_bin such as c(9,9,9) is caught earlier by the pars-length check at :340-341 and does error; the hypothesis' suggested probe is therefore the wrong one, but any post-check failure is silent.) triage.one_line: BDI logg and the thinning log q are different densities whose difference on a fixed tree depends on theta, but each is the correct density of its own sampler, so pairing each with f is valid; only simulate_tree()'s `log_q` label is ambiguous.
triage.evidence: On 30 BDI CR draws (20-tip tree, theta1 = (0.5, 0.3)) a standalone re-implementation of the BDI CR logg reproduces the package logg to 1.4e-12. On the same BDI data frames eval_logf's thinning logg minus the BDI logg ranges -5.0..+3.3 at theta1 and, at theta2 = (0.7, 0.2), the per-tree difference moves by -2.0..+2.6, i.e. it is theta-dependent and tree-dependent. logf - logg_bdi is identical across all 30 draws (sd 3.6e-13, value -39.335: the zero-variance CR property), whereas logf - logg_thin has sd 1.85 on the same draws. simulate_tree(method='bdi') returns log_q = -68.0,-87.6,-41.8 and method='thinning' returns -63.6,-48.4,-67.4 for the same tree and pars. No code path scores BDI trees with the thinning logg: bdi.R:684-691 discards eval_logf's logg; gam.R:513,783 and de.R use thinning trees. The hypothesis's claim that 'only one can be paired with f' is not right: each proposal density is paired with f for its own draws, which is all importance sampling requires.
triage.fix_sketch: Documentation only: in simulate_tree() state that log_q is the log-density of the proposal named by `method` (BDI conditional process vs thinning), that the two are not comparable across methods, and that eval_logf()'s logg is the thinning density and must not be paired with BDI draws. Optionally add a `method` attribute to the returned log_q.

triage.one_line: .bdi_iterate silently returns a non-converged mean-field rate field: at plausible high-turnover DD parameters the fixed-point iteration oscillates (delta 40-215 vs tol 1e-4) for 20 and even 100 iterations, and no flag or warning reaches the caller.
triage.evidence: Patched copy of .bdi_iterate (R/bdi.R:307-392) recording delta per iteration. 20-tip tree: mild DD (K=60) converges in 3 iterations, strong DD (K=20) in 6, over-saturated (K=10) in 12. 40-tip tree: lambda0=2, betaN=-0.05, mu=1 (K=40) stops at iter 20 with delta 39.1 (trajectory 30.8, 38.1, 49.9, ... 39.1, never decreasing); lambda0=3, betaN=-0.05, mu=1.5 (K=60 > 40 tips) stops at delta 83 and with max_iter=100 still ends at delta 87.7 (trajectory 38.8, 118, 138, 43.8, 137, ...); K=75 converges in 16. Gaussian closure on/off makes no difference. The function has no return slot for delta or the iteration count and `if (delta < tol) break` is the only exit; .augment_tree_bdi (bdi.R:648-655) uses whatever iterate 20 produced. Consequence is inefficiency rather than bias (logg is accumulated from the same rates the Gillespie uses), but under the K=40 field 0/50 draws had finite logf (linear-link lambda clipped to 0 at N >= K) and fhat was NaN, so the E-step is unusable and .mcem_bdi cannot tell why. The 'Cov ODE drops death cross-jumps' and 'E clipped to [0,tp]' parts of the hypothesis are documented approximations (bdi.R:222-226, 366) and inert under the gate (P/E slopes pinned to 0).
triage.fix_sketch: Return `converged`, `iterations` and `final_delta` from .bdi_iterate; warn (or message when verbose) in .augment_tree_bdi when converged is FALSE; damp the Picard update (Nhat <- (1-a)*Nhat + a*Nhat_new, a ~ 0.5) or use Anderson mixing so oscillating cases settle; expose max_iter/tol through the control list; record the flag in the mcem table so the diagnostics can show it.

triage.one_line: Under CR max_tries = sample_size, so max_missing overflow silently returns fewer trees (down to zero, which triggers the E-step failure path that perturbs pars toward the box centre) with rejected = 0 everywhere.
triage.evidence: 20-tip tree, pars8 = (0.5, mu 0.4): typical CR draws have 5-20 missing lineages. .augment_tree_bdi(sample_size = 50): max_missing = 2 returns 0 trees (fhat -Inf), 5 returns 2, 10 returns 23; the return list has no rejection count (names: trees, logf, logg, weights, fhat). .mcem_bdi with max_missing = 2: both iterations print 'E-step failed ... perturbed toward center', mcem table is NULL, stop_reason 'max_iter'. With max_missing = 10: num_trees = 18 and 27 of 50 requested, rejected = 0, final_IS$n_rejected = 0. Code: bdi.R:665 `max_tries <- if (is_cr) sample_size else 5L * sample_size`; bdi.R:669 `if (is.null(aug)) next` with no counter; bdi.R:804-807 and 851 hard-code every rejected_* field to 0L; bdi.R:699 fhat denominator is n_valid (overflow draws never enter the denominator, consistent with the thinning path per 01-map.md 1.5).
triage.fix_sketch: Count NULL returns in the draw loop (split into overflow vs survivor when the .bdi_augment_one return distinguishes them), return them as rejected_overruns / rejected in the .augment_tree_bdi list, propagate them into e_step, the mcem table and final_IS instead of the 0L literals; give CR the same 5*sample_size retry budget (overflow is not a survivor rejection); warn when n_valid < sample_size and when the shortfall is caused solely by max_missing.

triage.one_line: The DD-branch breaks (1-p < 1e-12, total < 1e-15) never caused a rejection in 1200 draws over four DD settings; every rejection at bdi.R:514 was a genuine survivor, and the total < 1e-15 break fires only with n_alive == 0 where the omitted survival term is < 1e-15 * (t1 - t).
triage.evidence: Patched copy of .bdi_augment_one tagging each break/return with its reason, 300 draws per setting on a 20-tip tree, model c(1,0,0), linear link. mild DD (K=60): 259 accepted clean, 41 reject_survivor. strong DD (K=20): 179 accepted clean, 77 accepted after a total-break with n_alive = 0, 44 reject_survivor. over-saturated (K=10): 280 accepted after total-break with n_alive = 0, 20 reject_survivor. over-saturated + mu 0.9: 288 / 12. Zero occurrences of omp-break or total-break with n_alive > 0 (min(1-p) on the grid was 0 at t = 0 in every setting, but the sampler never reached a time where the interpolated omp < 1e-12 with lineages alive). When total < 1e-15 with n_alive = 0 the skipped compensator is bounded by 1e-15 * segment length, negligible; when n_alive > 0 that cannot happen for the total term (mu_r = mu/(1-p) > 0 unless mu = 0). An omp-break with lineages alive would mean mu_r >= mu * 1e12, i.e. those lineages die essentially immediately, so treating it as a rejection would be conservative rather than wrong. Survivor rejection rates 4-15% are the intended approximate-Gillespie rejection (bdi.R:512-514 comment).
triage.fix_sketch: No change needed for correctness. Optional hardening: on omp < 1e-12 with n_alive > 0, kill all alive lineages at t (adding log(mu_r) per death) instead of breaking, and make the two breaks return an explicit reason so a rejection counter (H59) can attribute them.

triage.one_line: The seq(0L, -1L) zero-length assignment is harmless in R, and BDI augmentation/MCEM run on a 2-tip tree, but with no observed nodes every augmented lineage gets parent_id 0 which aliases the first augmented species (ids also start at 0), so .aug_to_Ltable attaches lineages to an extinct augmented parent and the returned tas has negative edges.
triage.evidence: `x[integer(0)] <- seq(0L,-1L)` raises no error or warning. tree '(A:5,B:5);' (brts = 5, bt empty): .augment_tree_bdi returns 20/20 trees with logf - logg = -4.667584 on every draw; .bdi_to_tree_df(list(), numeric(0), 5) returns just the closing row; DD path returns 10 trees, fhat -5.32; .mcem_bdi runs 3 iterations (num_trees 20, stop max_iter). But all augmented rows have parent_id = 0 (bdi.R:551-552 gives max(0L, integer(0)) = 0) while the observed id set is empty, and augmented species ids start at n_obs + i - 1 = 0 (bdi.R:549). In .aug_to_Ltable (simulate.R:437) `aug_labels[[as.character(pid)]]` then resolves parent 0 to the first augmented species: L-table row 5 has parent -4 (an augmented lineage that died at age 2.73) born at age 2.64, and DDD::L2phylo gives min edge -0.083; simulate_tree(method='bdi') on the 2-tip tree returns tas with 7 tips and min edge -2.95, whereas on a 20-tip tree the five tas have min edge +0.004. The thinning sampler on the same 2-tip tree returns 5 trees without error.
triage.fix_sketch: In .bdi_to_tree_df use parent_id = -1L when no observed branching precedes the birth (i.e. when which(bt_sorted <= birth) is empty), matching the thinning convention, and use seq_len(n_obs) - 1L for the observed ids; alternatively offset augmented ids so they never collide with parent ids. Add a 2-tip regression test asserting min(tas$edge.length) >= 0.

triage.one_line: The only expand/contract round-trip test uses mb=c(1,1,1), where .expand_pars is the identity, so the index arithmetic for partial models (100/001/101/010) is untested — though it is correct.

triage.one_line: Exported train_GAM() (and internal train_likelihood_GAM) call mgcv::gam with no requireNamespace guard while mgcv is only in Suggests; only .run_gam (estimate_rates method='gam') is guarded.
triage.evidence: DESCRIPTION:20-22 lists mgcv under Suggests. R/gam.R:67 and :909 call mgcv::gam unconditionally; R/inference.R:471-473 (.run_gam) is the only requireNamespace('mgcv') check. Emulating a machine without mgcv (unloadNamespace + trace on loadNamespace) makes train_GAM print its 'Training ... GAM' banner and then die with the raw error "no package called 'mgcv'" instead of an informative message. estimate_rates(method='gam') and the pipeline's gam stage (pipeline.R:178-185, tryCatch around estimate_rates) are covered by the .run_gam guard. Tests do not break: test-gam.R:3-11 stops on 'All parameter columns are constant' before reaching mgcv, and the fitting tests use skip_if_not_installed('mgcv'), so R CMD check passes without mgcv; the defect is the user-facing error from the exported function.

triage.one_line: Because skip_on_cran() precedes skip(), the four integration tests report the reason 'On CRAN' when run locally without NOT_CRAN set, hiding the real skip reason.
triage.evidence: tests/testthat/test-inference.R:71-72, 85-86, 98-99 and test-augment.R:4-5 each call skip_on_cran() then skip("C++ integration test ..."). H104.R runs test_file on both files with NOT_CRAN unset: all four tests are skipped with 'Reason: On CRAN'. With Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN='true') the same tests report the intended messages ('C++ integration test: run locally with devtools::test(filter=...)', 'mc_loglik integration test skipped locally to avoid long runtime'). Note devtools::test() sets NOT_CRAN=true, so the misleading reason appears only under plain testthat::test_dir/test_file, R CMD check, or Rscript; the tests never run in either case because the second skip() is unconditional (README:43 acknowledges they run nowhere).
triage.fix_sketch: Drop the redundant skip_on_cran() in front of every unconditional skip() (the skip already covers CRAN), or replace both with a single gate such as `skip_if_not(identical(Sys.getenv('EMPHASIS_RUN_INTEGRATION'), 'true'), 'set EMPHASIS_RUN_INTEGRATION=true to run C++ integration tests')` so the tests are actually runnable on demand and the reason is always accurate.

triage.one_line: diagnose_cem/diagnose_mcem error on a fit whose best_IS/final_IS lacks ESS, both return visibly although documented as invisible, and diagnose_mcem pairs 2 compact par names with 8 par[0-9]+ trace columns; the recomputed-ESS and B=200 sub-claims are not defects.
triage.evidence: Ran dev/audit/checks/H86.R on a 15-tip CR tree (cem: max_iter=2, 6 particles, 3 trees; mcem: max_iter=2, sample_size=20). Results: `diagnose_cem(fit, plot=FALSE)` withVisible()$visible = TRUE (doc at R/diagnostics.R:69 says invisibly; body ends with `structure(...)` at :305-315, no invisible()); same for diagnose_mcem (:354 vs :533-541). Removing `$ESS` from best_IS -> diagnose_cem errors 'argument is of length zero' (R/diagnostics.R:142 `if (!is.na(bi$ESS))` on NULL); removing final_IS$ESS -> diagnose_mcem errors 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed' (:409). ESS stored in fit (13.188) equals emphasis:::.ess_from_lw(lw) recomputed (13.188), so 'taken from fit rather than recomputed' has no numerical consequence. MCEM trace data frame has 8 par columns (R/emphasis.R:97 names the 8-vector par1..par8) while names(x$pars) has 2 entries; diagnose_mcem sets n_par <- length(par_cols) = 8 (:424) and labels panels with par_names[j] (:457), so panels 3..8 get NA labels and the inactive zero parameters are plotted. 'B=200' string in print.mcem_diagnostics (:579) matches the hard-coded B = 200L in R/emphasis.R:141 and R/de.R:884, so it is consistent, only unparameterised. Note the current CEM/MCEM code always populates ESS, so the NULL case reaches only hand-built or legacy objects.
triage.fix_sketch: Wrap the return values in invisible() (or change the @return docs); guard ESS with `ess <- if (is.null(bi$ESS)) .ess_from_lw(bi$lw) else bi$ESS` and use isTRUE(!is.na(ess)); in diagnose_mcem contract the trace columns to the active parameters (use .contract_pars / model_bin from x$model) so par_cols and par_names agree; replace the literal 'B=200' by a stored `n_boot` field.

triage.one_line: compare_models errors with two same-model fits when all carry loglik_var (label-indexed AIC gives a length-2 T_ij) and errors on a double-typed n_pars; estimate_rates itself always stores an integer n_pars, so the second path needs a hand-built fit.
triage.evidence: Ran dev/audit/checks/H87.R with synthetic emphasis_fit objects. Two unnamed CR fits with loglik_var -> 'number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length' (R/inference.R:933 `tab$AIC[tab$model == nms[i]]` returns 2 values because both labels are 'CR' from .model_label). Same fits without variance -> OK (pairwise block skipped). n_pars stored as double 2 and 4 -> vapply error "values must be type 'integer', but FUN(X[[1]]) result is type 'double'" (R/inference.R:910). estimate_rates sets n_pars <- length(pars) (R/inference.R:816), typeof integer, so fits from estimate_rates never hit the vapply error; pipeline.R:318 copies that integer. `compare_models(list(a, b))` as literally phrased errors 'requires at least two fitted models' because the signature is `...`, not a list. compare_models is @keywords internal and not exported.

triage.one_line: License spec, checkout@v3, missing coverage/--as-cran are as described, but the emphasis.Rcheck/ and tarball sub-claim is refuted: R CMD build excludes both by default and the syst_biol trigger names an existing branch.
triage.evidence: DESCRIPTION:11 is `License: file LICENSE` with a full MIT text in LICENSE; tools:::.check_package_license() on the built DESCRIPTION returned an empty result, so R CMD check emits no NOTE, but the spec is not the CRAN-required `MIT + file LICENSE` with the two-line template (this is a CRAN-policy issue, not a check failure). .Rbuildignore contains `^\.\.Rcheck$` (matches only the stray `..Rcheck` dir) and no tarball pattern; however building from a full copy of the checkout that contained both emphasis.Rcheck/ and emphasis_0.4.tar.gz (/tmp/h88b, `R CMD build --no-build-vignettes --no-manual`) produced a 107-entry tarball with zero entries matching 'Rcheck' or 'tar.gz', top level = DESCRIPTION, LICENSE, NAMESPACE, README.md only — R's built-in exclusions cover them. .github/workflows/main.yml:37 uses actions/checkout@v3 (Node16-deprecated), args = c('--no-manual','--no-build-vignettes','--ignore-vignettes') with no --as-cran, and there is no covr/test-coverage job. `git branch -a` shows a local `syst_biol` branch, so that trigger is stale-looking but not dead. Note .Rbuildignore is locally modified (uncommitted `^dev$` line).
triage.repro_script: code-read (tarball test: rsync checkout to /tmp/h88b and R CMD build; not kept as a checks/ script because it needs no package load)
triage.fix_sketch: Set `License: MIT + file LICENSE` and reduce LICENSE to the YEAR/COPYRIGHT HOLDER template (keep the full text in LICENSE.md, build-ignored); bump to actions/checkout@v4, add `--as-cran` to the check args and an r-lib test-coverage workflow; drop `syst_biol` from the trigger list once that branch is merged; optionally add `^emphasis\.Rcheck$` and `^emphasis_.*\.tar\.gz$` to .Rbuildignore for explicitness, and commit the `^dev$` line.

triage.one_line: train_GAM and train_likelihood_GAM print one cat() line unconditionally; neither has a verbose argument, so expect_silent fails.
triage.evidence: Ran dev/audit/checks/H89.R (60 CR forward sims, max_t=3, max_tries=0). capture.output(train_GAM(...)) returns 1 line: 'Training univariate survival GAM on 60 simulations (survival rate: 0.55 )...' (R/gam.R:65-66); `'verbose' %in% names(formals(train_GAM))` is FALSE. emphasis:::train_likelihood_GAM prints 'Training univariate likelihood GAM on 60 grid points...' (R/gam.R:907-908), no verbose formal either. testthat::expect_silent(train_GAM(...)) fails with 'Actual noise: output.' Callers that do honour verbose (auto_bounds R/gam.R:372, .run_gam) still get the line when the user passes verbose = FALSE.
triage.fix_sketch: Add `verbose = FALSE` (or getOption('emphasis.verbose')) to both signatures, wrap the cat() in `if (verbose)` and switch to message() so it is suppressible; pass verbose through from auto_bounds and .run_gam; add expect_silent tests.

triage.one_line: Four distinct attempt/overflow budgets exist for augmentation and forward simulation, max_tries is silently dropped on the conditional path, and the failure counters differ per path; it is a documentation/consistency gap, not a wrong result.
triage.evidence: Code read. Budgets: (1) forward simulate_tree retries `max_tries` times at R level and always passes 0 to C++ (R/simulate.R:206-208); (2) `.augment_tree_internal` defaults maxN = max(2000, 200*sample_size) (R/simulate.R:475); (3) `.run_mcem` defaults maxN = max(2000, 10*sample_size) only when NULL, while estimate_rates_control already sets 2000 for mcem (R/inference.R:117, 365); (4) CEM control maxN = 10 with a different meaning (R/inference.R:126); (5) BDI uses max_tries = sample_size (CR) or 5*sample_size (DD) (R/bdi.R:665). simulate_tree accepts `max_tries` (R/simulate.R:134) and forwards it in the batch recursion (:157-159), but `.sim_tree_conditional` (:333-338) has no such argument, so on the conditional path it is ignored without warning. Failure reporting: forward returns survival_prob = 1/n_attempts (:211); conditional returns tas = NULL/log_q = NA with no attempt count (:367-370); MCEM/CEM report `rejected`/`n_rejected` from the C++ counters; BDI shortfalls have no counter (see H59). No incorrect number arises from this, hence minor.
triage.fix_sketch: Document one `maxN` meaning ('total augmentation attempts, must exceed sample_size') in estimate_rates_control and derive every default from one helper (e.g. `.default_maxN(sample_size)`); either thread `max_tries` into .sim_tree_conditional (as a retry count for empty draws) or drop it from the documented arguments for tree != NULL and warn when supplied; return a common `attempts`/`n_rejected` pair from simulate_tree, .augment_tree_bdi and the E-step so failure statistics are comparable.

triage.one_line: The code fixes the conditioning event as {both crown clades alive at T} AND {N < max_lin} and uses the same cond_fun in the M-step, the CEM fhat and the reported loglik; measured, that event equals DDD's cond=1 event within MC error (max_lin truncation contributed 0 at max_lin=500), while the GAM itself adds up to ~0.12 absolute error in P_surv on a 214-point training set.
triage.evidence: Code: train_GAM labels survived = (status == 'done') (R/gam.R:37); general_tree.hpp:175 sets maxN_exceeded when N >= max_N and :290 sets extinction when N1 < 1 || N2 < 1, so 'done' = both crown lineages alive at T and never reaching max_lin (auto_bounds uses max_lin = max(20 n_tips, 500), R/gam.R:163). .build_cond_fun returns log max(predict_survival, 1e-300) (R/inference.R:333-344); the same cond_fun object is passed to .run_mcem/.run_cem (:805-808) and subtracted from the reported MCEM loglik (:819-822) and the CEM fhat_best (R/de.R:869-870), so M-step and reported likelihood condition on one event. Ran dev/audit/checks/H91.R: 400 CR sims per theta at T=5, max_lin=500: done fraction vs analytic (1-P_ext)^2 vs DDD::bd_loglik cond=1 normaliser (exp(l_cond0 - l_cond1)) = 0.647/0.676/0.676, 0.235/0.263/0.263, 0.110/0.112/0.112, 0.065/0.080/0.080; too_large fraction 0.000 everywhere. A survival GAM trained on 214 LHS points predicted 0.552, 0.260, 0.141, 0.131 at the same four points (analytic 0.676, 0.263, 0.112, 0.080), i.e. the approximation error of the smooth, not the event, is the larger discrepancy (up to 0.5 nats in log P_surv). Whether the README's 'conditional likelihood' is meant to include the max_lin truncation and to tolerate GAM error of this size is the author's call; the interaction with the M-step penalty scale is H4.
triage.fix_sketch: State the event explicitly in the train_GAM/estimate_rates docs ('both crown clades extant at T and fewer than max_lin lineages'); for CR (and DD via DDD::dd_loglik cond=1) offer an analytic/numeric P_surv instead of the GAM, or raise n_gam and report the GAM's calibration error; add a test comparing predict_survival with (1-P_ext)^2 on CR.

triage.one_line: The C++ max_tries retry loop in simulate_div_tree_cpp is dead from R: its only caller passes 0L and does its own retry loop.
triage.evidence: grep over R/ and tests/: the sole call is R/simulate.R:207 `simulate_div_tree_cpp(pars8, model_bin, max_t, max_lin_i, 0L, link_int)` inside an R-level `while (raw$status != 'done' && n_attempts <= max_tries_i)` loop (:204-209) that counts attempts to compute survival_prob = 1/n_attempts. With 0 the C++ `while (... tries < max_tries)` at src/div_tree.cpp:33-38 never iterates. The wrapper is not exported (NAMESPACE has no simulate_div_tree_cpp entry) and no test calls it, yet RcppExports.R:12 and div_tree.cpp:13 document max_tries as 'Maximum retries after extinction or overflow'. The R loop exists because the C++ loop does not report the number of tries, which survival_prob needs.
triage.fix_sketch: Either remove the max_tries parameter and loop from simulate_div_tree_cpp (update RcppExports via roxygen/compileAttributes on the next documented build) or make the C++ loop the single implementation by returning `tries` in the result list and deleting the R loop; in both cases document which one owns the retry semantics.

triage.one_line: At rho = 1 no augmented lineage ever receives the unsampled sentinel: 0 of 30,000 trees (mu = 0.001, 0.3, 3; ~700k extinct insertions) had t_ext == 5e10 or a non-sentinel t_ext >= T.
triage.evidence: model.hpp:217-235: at rho_ == 1 the p_unsampled branch is skipped and extinction_time returns t_spec + trunc_exp(remaining, mu), where trunc_exp (model_helpers.hpp:157-165) rejects result > upper, so ext_time <= T with equality only on a measure-zero draw or a last-ulp rounding of t_spec + r. dev/audit/checks/H49.log: 'mu=0.3: trees=10000 aug_extinct=259502 t_ext==5e10: 0 t_ext>=T: 0 nonfinite lw: 0' and the same zeros for mu=0.001 and mu=3. Even if the rounding case fired, sampling_prob line 308 adds log(n*lambda*(1-rho)) = log(0) and eval_logf adds n_unsamp*log(1-rho) (model.hpp:466), so lw is non-finite and E_step.cpp:94 discards the draw; it cannot enter the likelihood as an extra extant tip.
triage.fix_sketch: Optional hardening only: in do_augment_tree_cont route to insert_unsampled_species only when `rho_ < 1 && ext_time >= b`, and clamp `ext_time = std::min(ext_time, std::nextafter(b, 0.0))` otherwise, so the rho = 1 path can never emit a 5e10 node.

triage.one_line: trunc_exp's rejection loop does not stall in practice: with gamma0 = 0 (mu clamped to 1e-10) augment_trees runs at 0.3 ms/tree, faster than with gamma0 = 0.3 (0.9 ms/tree), because the thinning rate itself is proportional to (1 - e^{-mu r}) and cancels the 1/(1 - e^{-mu r}) expected rejections.
triage.evidence: model_helpers.hpp:157-165 is the rejection sampler as described (acceptance 1 - e^{-mu*upper}, ~1e-9 at mu = 1e-10, r = 6). But nh_rate (model.hpp:238-252) proposes candidates at n*lambda*(1 - rho*e^{-mu_eff (T-t)}) ~ n*lambda*mu*r at rho = 1, so E[calls] x E[iterations per call] = O(n*lambda*T) independent of mu; at rho < 1, p_unsampled = (1-rho)e^{-mu r}/(1 - rho e^{-mu r}) -> 1 so trunc_exp is reached with probability ~mu*r*rho/(1-rho). H50.log: 'gamma0=0 rho=1: 2000 trees in 0.62s (0.3 ms/tree); mean extinct/tree=0.000', 'gamma0=1e-06 rho=1: 0.3 ms/tree', 'gamma0=0 rho=0.8: 0.5 ms/tree, mean unsampled/tree=11.68', 'gamma0=-2 rho=1: 0.3 ms/tree' vs 'gamma0=0.3 rho=1: 0.9 ms/tree'. The worst case per single call (1e9 spins) exists in principle but is entered with probability ~1e-9 per candidate.
triage.fix_sketch: Replace the loop with the inverse CDF: `const double u = std::uniform_real_distribution<>()(reng); return -std::log1p(u * std::expm1(-rate * upper)) / rate;` (O(1), exact, no dependence on mu*upper); keep a guard for rate*upper < 1e-12 returning u*upper.

triage.one_line: insert_species' dirty-range loop `for (++first; first->brts < t_ext; ++first)` (augment_tree.cpp:101) has no tree.end() guard and terminates only because the caller guarantees t_ext < b == tree.back().brts; a direct call with t_ext > T walks past the end (UB).
triage.evidence: Code read. augment_tree.cpp:94-103: the loop's sole stop condition is a node with brts >= t_ext; the closing sentinel node (E_step.cpp:34, brts = T) satisfies it iff t_ext <= T. The only caller (augment_tree.cpp:167-187) tests `if (ext_time >= b)` first and sends those to insert_unsampled_species, so in the current call graph t_ext < b always holds and the sentinel bounds the loop; extinction_time (model.hpp:217-235) also returns <= T at rho = 1 and T+1 at rho < 1, both routed correctly. No runtime failure is reachable; the safety is a two-file invariant with no assert. A C++ unit test cannot be added under the no-compile rule.
triage.fix_sketch: Make the invariant local: `for (++first; first != tree.end() && first->brts < t_ext; ++first)` plus `assert(t_ext < tree.back().brts)` at the top of insert_species; optionally have insert_species take the sentinel time and clamp.

triage.one_line: Float32 event times produce no zero-length edges and no duplicate branching times in the package's 10-1000-tip regime; collisions appear only in simulated trees of 5k-20k tips (49 duplicated branching times and 602 duplicated L-table birth ages across 325k nodes), and the bernoulli(NaN) path is not reached through floating fallback.
triage.evidence: general_tree.hpp:70-79 stores start_date/tip_start/end_date as float and t as float; granularity at t ~ 100 is 100*2^-23 = 1.19e-5. H52.log (40 trees, cr pars c(0.1,0.02), max_t = 100, 119-21,848 tips): zero_edges = 0 in every tree, min_edge = 7.63e-6 (exactly one float ulp), dup_bt = 0 for every tree under ~4,000 tips and 1-9 for 6k-21k tips; all forward dates are exactly float32-representable (fraction 1). The NaN route requires rate_sum == 0 at the new t (general_tree.hpp:212-256), which cannot come from float rounding; probing the linear link with a strongly negative D slope (H52_nan.R, 400 simulations, model 'd', pars c(0.8,-0.6,0,0) and c(0.8,-0.6,0.5,-0.6)) gave only 'done'/'extinct' statuses, no error. Nearest-value parent matching (simulate.R:428) can only be ambiguous when two observed birth ages coincide, which needs the 5k+-tip regime.
triage.fix_sketch: Change gbranch::{start_date, tip_start, end_date} and general_div::t to double (rnd_t and the arithmetic already use double); in simulate.R:428 match parent by id/label instead of nearest birth age; in general_tree.hpp guard `if (rate_sum <= 0.0) { break_type = finished; break; }` before the weighted selection.

triage.one_line: Augmentation cost grows superlinearly in augmented-tree size (empirical exponent 1.5-1.9 over 75-1,845 nodes; 2 ms -> 176 ms per tree) because calculate_pendant_pd is O(N) and is called once per node in compute_pendant_pd pass 2 and once per thinning candidate in nh_rate, even for model 'cr' where pd is unused.
triage.evidence: model_helpers.hpp:216-229 scans the whole prefix of the tree; augment_tree.cpp:56-58 calls it for every node (O(N^2)); model.hpp:242 calls it unconditionally on every nh_rate evaluation (2 per interval + 1 per candidate), independent of model_bin. H53.log (40 tips, cr): 75 nodes -> 1.05 ms/tree, 249 -> 3.6, 310 -> 5.0 (exponent 1.51). H53_scale.log (25-200 tips, mu 0.1/0.3): 132 nodes -> 2.1 ms, 645 -> 23.5, 897 -> 40.4, 1845 -> 175.8 ms/tree (exponent 1.93 over all points). A 200-tip tree with 1e4 missing lineages (~2e4 nodes) extrapolates to ~10-20 s per augmented tree, i.e. minutes per E-step of 200 trees.
triage.fix_sketch: Skip the pd computation when model_bin[1] == 0 && model_bin[2] == 0 (pd unused); otherwise maintain P(t) incrementally: keep a running (n_alive, sum_tip_start) pair per segment so P(t) = n_alive*t - sum_tip_start in O(1) (the forward simulator already does this at general_tree.hpp:212), updating the two sums on each insertion in O(log N) via the sorted node list.

triage.one_line: The critical branch of .bdi_integral_cr is wrong (returns 4.433 where the lam -> mu limit is 8.143 for t1=1,t2=3,n=2,k=3,tp=5,lam=0.5), but it is dead in effect because at lam == mu .bdi_p_cr returns 0/0 = NaN and the BDI Gillespie loop crashes ('missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed'), which .mcem_bdi/.sim_tree_conditional catch as an E-step failure; the general formula keeps full precision down to d = 1e-14.
triage.evidence: R/bdi.R:39-45 uses I_lam = log(a1/a2), I_mu = lam*dt + log(a2/a1) with the comment 'p = lam*(tp-t)/(1+lam*(tp-t))' reversed (the limit of bdi.R:16-19 is p = 1/(1+lam*tau)). Correct integrals: I_lam = lam*dt - log(a1/a2), I_mu = lam*dt + log((tp-t1)/(tp-t2)). H54.log: 'critical limit closed form = 8.1425734963; numeric integrate at d=0 = 8.1425734963; code critical branch = 4.4327906486'; general branch |code - limit| = 8.7e-4 (d=1e-4), 1.6e-9 (1e-10), 1.6e-13 (1e-14), so no precision loss; at d = 1e-15 and 0 the code jumps to 4.433. Reachability: .augment_tree_bdi(brts, pars = c(0.5,0.5), model_bin = c(0,0,0)) errors inside .bdi_augment_one (NaN from .bdi_p_cr at bdi.R:451), while d = 1e-9 and 1e-3 run normally (sd(lw) 7.5e-7 and 2.3e-10). estimate_rates with init lam == mu therefore logs 'E-step failed ... perturbed toward center' rather than returning a wrong value.
triage.fix_sketch: In .bdi_p_cr add `if (abs(lam0-mu0) < 1e-12) return(1/(1 + lam0*(tp - t)))`; in .bdi_integral_cr replace the critical branch by `I_lam <- lam0*(t2-t1) - log(a1/a2); I_mu <- lam0*(t2-t1) + log((tp-t1)/(tp-t2))` (Inf when t2 == tp and n > 0, matching the general branch); widen the switch threshold to ~1e-12 and add a unit test comparing against integrate() across d.

triage.one_line: .augment_tree_bdi accepts an 8-element pars with non-zero slots 3/4 and no internal gate (both model_bin (0,0,0) and (1,0,1) ran), .bdi_lam reads them as slopes on P and E (1.6) while the C++ likelihood reads them as beta_M, beta_D (0.85), and the Gaussian-closure ODE changes only Ehat (max 0.040) while Nhat and p are bit-identical, so it is inert whenever slot 4 is 0, which .bdi_supported plus .expand_pars guarantee on every public path.
triage.evidence: R/bdi.R:108-116 (`pars8[3]*P + pars8[4]*E`) vs model.hpp:148-156, 193-201 (`pars[2]*M + pars[3]*D`, M = pd/n, D = E - M). bdi.R:634-638 takes any length-8 vector verbatim; the only gates are outside (inference.R:359, simulate.R:345 via .bdi_supported, which requires model_bin[2] == model_bin[3] == 0 so .expand_pars pins slots 3/4 to 0: H55.log 'expanded DD pars8: 0.6 -0.01 0 0 0.2 0 0 0'). H55.log: '8-elem pars, CR: accepted, 5 trees'; '8-elem pars, model (1,0,1): accepted, 5 trees'; 'R .bdi_lam(...): 1.6  C++ convention: 0.85'; '.bdi_iterate closure TRUE vs FALSE: max|Nhat diff| = 0, max|p diff| = 0, max|Ehat diff| = 0.040; vN nonzero TRUE, cNP nonzero TRUE'. Since Ehat and Phat enter rates only through slots 3/4, .bdi_solve_meanvar_forward (bdi.R:231-284), the P_miss state and the Taylor correction (bdi.R:338-366) cannot affect any draw or logg under reachable configurations.
triage.fix_sketch: Inside .augment_tree_bdi call `stopifnot(.bdi_supported(model_bin, link), pars8[3] == 0, pars8[4] == 0, pars8[7] == 0, pars8[8] == 0)` (or error with the same message as the public gate); either delete .bdi_solve_meanvar_forward and the Phat/Ehat plumbing or rewrite .bdi_lam/.bdi_mu in the (N, M, D) basis (`eta <- p[1] + p[2]*N + p[3]*P/N + p[4]*(E - P/N)`) and extend the gate when the mean-field D closure is validated.

triage.one_line: rsbplx.cpp:144 throws on every negative nlopt_result (incl. NLOPT_ROUNDOFF_LIMITED=-4) and emphasis.R:45-70 catches any em_cpp error as an 'E-step failure' (doubles maxN, perturbs pars); but no -4 was observed in 70 fits, even with xtol_rel=0 or 1e-14.

triage.one_line: tbb::task_scheduler_init is a TBB-2019 API that RcppParallel 5.1.11.2 still ships (removed in oneTBB 2021, so a system-oneTBB build breaks) and the is_threadsafe guard is inert; but an R error thrown from the conditional inside the nlopt call stack unwinds cleanly on this platform (5/5 runs, package stays usable).
triage.evidence: Installed RcppParallel 5.1.11.2, include/tbb/tbb_stddef.h: TBB_VERSION_MAJOR 2019, TBB_VERSION_MINOR 0, no oneapi/ dir (dev/audit/checks/H67.R). M_step.cpp:76 guard is commented out, but model.hpp:113 `is_threadsafe() const { return true; }` so the guard would be a no-op anyway. objective() calls `psd->conditional->operator()(pars)` (an Rcpp::Function) after the parallel_reduce, on the calling thread, from inside remp_optimize's C frames. Empirical: rconditional that calls stop() on its 3rd invocation -> em_cpp returns 'R error: boom from R conditional' in 5/5 runs (calls=3 each), warnings inside the conditional surface as 44 R warnings, and a subsequent plain fit returns nlopt=4. The unwind through nlopt's C frames leaks nlopt_optimize's internal allocations but did not corrupt state here.
triage.fix_sketch: Replace task_scheduler_init with `tbb::task_arena arena(num_threads); arena.execute([&]{ ... })` (or tbb::global_control), delete the dead guard line, and wrap the conditional call in a try/catch that records the failure in nlopt_f_data and returns +inf (or calls nlopt_force_stop) so nlopt returns NLOPT_FORCED_STOP and the C++ side rethrows after nlopt has cleaned up.

triage.evidence: Code: the outer `if (!stop)` and the inner `if (!stop)` (E_step.cpp:97-104) are read without the mutex; the assignment at :107 is `stop = (size == N)`, not `stop |= ...`; the `else` branch at :110 increments rejected_zero_weights regardless of stop; the tbb::task_arena at :60 is constructed but parallel_for is not run inside it (global arena; grainsize=maxN/num_threads keeps 1 thread serial). fhat at :134 divides sum over ALL kept trees by S_completed = N + rejected_zero_weights. Empirical (dev/audit/checks/H68_b.R, 25 tips, ~N model, N=100, maxN=3000): threads=1 -> 100 trees x10, fhat -48.64 (sd 0.26), zero-w 0.4; threads=4 -> 100 x10, fhat -48.87; threads=8 -> trees 2628,100,2574,100,100,100,100,2277,2540,1922, fhat mean -47.20 (sd 1.69), zero-w 5.5, time 790 ms vs 149. H68.R (augment_trees, N=100, maxN=5000, threads=8) similarly returned 100-4359 trees. Default num_threads=1 (inference.R:105) so default fits are unaffected; any num_threads>1 run is.
triage.fix_sketch: Inside the mutex: `if (static_cast<int>(E.trees.size()) < N) { push...; if (E.trees.size() == N) stop = true; } else { /* drop, count as discarded */ }`; never assign stop=false. Count post-stop rejections separately or skip counting once stop is set, so attempts = N + rejected_* holds; use arena.execute() around the parallel_for so num_threads is honoured; move tree copying out of the critical section (copy into a thread-local buffer, then swap under the lock).
